review_text:
Bentota beach, otherwise known as Ventura Beach, is a beautiful white sandy beach with clear waters that are quite rough and strong at times. We didn't go in the water but people were in swimming, and body boarding. 

We were surprised the beach wasn't lined with beachfront restaurants but there are sunbeds with umbrellas lining the beach that also serve food. 
We got sunbeds from "Nice Place", which was 500 lkr for the day Inc umbrella, then also had some beer, a delicious wrap, and other snacks throughout the day. They also tuk tuked us back to hotel for 250 lkr too. Very reasonable.

review_text:
Bentota beach is lovely. Fine sand gently shelving into a warm sea. For most of the day there were only a handful of people on the beach but come a weekend evening the locals come with their families for a dip and the atmosphere is fantastic and friendly.
DO check out the warning flags as there are some strong currents. Near the Taj hotel on the north side where the beach dog legs to the south there is safer bathing. You can walk for miles seeing the fishermen folding their nets and hauling outriggers from the sea whilst singing songs. If you are going for a walk on the beach take water as there are no beach bars but you can occasionally walk through the trees to a hotel bar. Beware the sun is reflected from the sand and you will burn very easily as there is always a good breeze.
We had no hassle from any touts.

review_text: I am staying at The Taj on Bentota beach and reckon this beach has a lot going for it. By The Taj there is a little cove that has the sun loungers and stuff if that's what you want. To the right and left as wide expanses of beach with few people on them. Sure you can find isolated places with loungers and umbrellas but most of the beach is untouched. The sand is lovely and soft. The sea at the moment is lovely and warm but it is very 'wavy' and not good for swimming, its fun though! This is why I don't give it 5 stars. There are a very few local sellers on the beach but they are very few and far between and do not hassle.

review_text:
I just don't get why people rave about Bentota. Yes, the beach is huge and absolutely beautiful and unspoilt BUT there are no beach bars/restaurants, no toilets, no loungers/parasols. Unless you are staying at one of the big resorts and want to pay top dollar. 
Personally, I like to wander along the beach and choose a nice cafe/bar/restaurant to stop for a bite to eat and/or drink but you just can't do that here. Not that I'm an advocate of the over-populated tourist trap but it's nice to have a choice.
Additionally, the surf is so strong that it is not safe for even the most confident of swimmers.

review_text:
Great beach (the best we've seen in Sri Lanka, out of 4 or 5) IF: 1) you don't want bars and annoying vendors on the beach, 2) you don't like crowds, 3) you like fine-grained sand and a clean beach, 4) especially, if you like swimming Â– not wading, but really swimming. There is a rock between the bay and the sea, it's about 900 meters from the beach, so it's a great swim.  When the sea is calm, you can swim very near the rock and see all kinds of fish (not much of coral reef, though, and whatever there is is dead).  When the sea is not so calm, be very careful Â– I stayed at least 10Â–20 meters away from the nearest visible rock, and I could still see some rocks beneath me.  

The downsides: 1) The sea is very opaque (cloudy) Â– you can't see further than 1 meter, perhaps a little more.  This is because of the very fine sand floating in the sea (near the beach) and, above all, because of microscopic algae making the water green.  2) On the way from the beach to the rock, there is an area where somewhat dirty-looking foam gathers Â– you might want to swim around it.  3) Of course, as transpires from the above, if you like beach partying, this is not a beach for you.  4) The waves can be strong, so I am not sure it's a good beach for small kids.

review_text:
Sri Lanka is a island country in Indian ocean. In Sri lanka trip you can get hill station, national park and sea beach, Metro life at a time.

Season for travel.
From mid September you can visit Sri lanka. November December and January are peak season in Sri lanka.

In the sri lanka vacation on 3rd day we went to bentota from Kandy. It is a beach destination in West coast of Sri Lanka. There we took bentota river boat ride. The boat has gone through mangrove forest. There are lot of water sports agent. You can easily book it. The cost of boat ride 10 USD per person. It was 40 minutes boat journey. There are lot of sports activity like speed boat riding, jet ski etc. We spent that night in bentota hotel. Bentota beach is very silent and clear and beautiful, but for taking sea bath it is quite risky. If tourist want beautiful but silence beach destination, then Bentota is the best option. 

Next day I took another boat ride. That is Madhu Ganga boat ride. The cost was 10 USD per person. This is 2 hr boat journey. After boat ride we moved to Galle. There we have seen light house, some old architecture. We came back in bentota hotel. Bentota to Galle distance is 75km. It will takes 2 hr. Galle is also a good place to hang out.

review_text:
This beach is really nice and clean. Clear white sand. Sri Lanka is very warm most of the time, hence be warned of this. They charge so much money for small things from tourists. In order to hire 2 beach lounger and one small umbrella, it costed us 3000 rupees. Same thing in Kerala, India beach only costed 300 rupees. So be warned of this.
There are some private areas of beach which is not so expensive, so worth mentioning to your driver, which beach you would like to go to.

I'm not a huge fan of swimming in large bodies of water because I live in Egypt & the Mediterranean is really cold with rough waves. at least in my experience. 
I was especially worried because I was gonna swim in an ocean instead of a sea, something I hadn't done before. 
but I was pleasantly surprised. the ocean was warm & the current was weak. the ground also isn't very steep, we had to walk a good while before the water reached our necks. 
the beach itself was very nice. the seating & service were alright but we spent most of our time in the water.
either way, it was really nice & I recommend it.

This showcases BawaÂ’s wide  architectural influences ranging from Bali to ancient Sri Lankan monuments. Inside the hotel has the signature of Geoffrey Bawa and the period it was constructed in, but in a modern and functional representation. 

The lead architect Channa Daswatte has done an amazing job, not only to archive an iconic construction but also through his brilliance, make it a fresh, modern and functional. review_text:
Beautiful beach- pristine sand. 
The Northern end of the beach has a lot of foliage which one should be careful of due the insects, mainly big mosquitoes.
The beach itself is great,surf crashing in , however, the currents are a mite strong. Those wishing to go deeper should exercise caution.
Lots of activities as in motor gliding, helicopter rides, and a wide expanse to lie down sun bathe and get an even suntan. 
One of the most beautiful beaches i have seen, extremely clean and neat.

Loved the beach and we had a great stay in Avani Bentota.

There are a lot of activities that could be over the back and all centers are within few minutes of walking.

If you are into diving or swimming try to get that as early as possible as the sea gets to be rough a bit towards the afternoon onwards.

Could not love it more and looking forward to my next visit.

review_text:
Bentota is one among the serene beaches in Srilanka, filled with numerous home stays and star accommodations. It is a calm and quiet beach if you are there in November I'm not quiet sure about the other months. You could do some surfing here, there are boards for hire and trainers to teach you some basic stuff.

The route to the beach is lined with great restaurants which mostly have amazing sea food options, I would suggest not to invest on buying Gems here since I feel like its a bit over priced and commercial.

There aren't too many shops so its just perfect to stay in the area and completely enjoy all the time on the beach.

review_text:
What a gem, more or less had the beach to ourselves. 
Long sandy and clean beach. 
Great sunsets from the loft bar. 
The sea is not for children in December, don't know about any other months but it's got large waves and strong changing currents.
The sea is warm and if you respect it you can have great fun in the waves but don't go in alone and don't go out of your depth. 
Sun lounger hire x2 with brolly 1000 rupees with a coconut or two thrown in.

review_text:
I love a good walk on the beach and Bentota's beach is beautiful - long, wide and very clean. But once you've walked up and then walked back, that's just about all there is to do. There didn't appear to be any facilities directly on the beach. Nobody so much as offered us a sun bed or tried to sell us a meal or drinks. Most of the restaurants were in the hotels that line the beach and many had 'residents only' signs which didn't encourage us to visit.
Beautiful but such a shame there's not much there. We wondered if we were just too early in the season but were told that this is pretty much all there is.

review_text:
Very nice beach. 
BUT watch for the guys located at the beach close to The Surf Hotel. They offer car sightseeing and fishing tours by boat. We had a nice experience with the car sightseeing - payed 7000 slr for a 7 hours tour to Galle. Two days later they offered us a three hours fishing tour without giving a price. We could pay what we wanted based on the tour experience. 
The trip was a disaster, run by two young teenagers. When we came back, the managers put a hard pressure on us to pay 100 US$ - or 17000 slr. I got angry and payed 5000 slr. 
My advice: Stay away from these swindlers!

review_text:
There are lots of different parts to Bentota Beach, there is a stretch that has a lagoon on one side, then it sprawls down alongside the road, so there are lots of different places to get to it from.
Whichever you choose itÂ’s almost deserted, or if not you wonÂ’t need to search far to get a section to yourself, the sea can be rough but if you search there are little coves that are relatively guarded.

The northern area with the lagoon is very shallow and you can walk out quite a distance without any trouble but you still have to be careful of waves and currents dependant on time of year.

One of the better and quietest beaches we found.

review_text: Beautiful water, un-littered beach, but so many boats and the fuel fumes were nausiating and spoilt the ambiance and experience. Environmentalists and greenies would shudder. Given that most of the coral is dead and yet to regenerate, the glass bottom boat rides should be stopped. I have seen these corals as a kid in the early 70s it was absolutely alive, vibrantly colourful and beautiful. I did another trip in around 2004 the coral was dead, save for two tiny patches where regrowth was starting, the entire coral garden was chalky grey. The Hikkaduwa beach could benefit from environmentalists focus and action.

review_text:
An excellent beach, wide, clean and featuring crystal clear, warm water. 

We enjoyed snorkeling towards the north end where the reef offers protection from the surf.

Elsewhere, the waters were a bit tougher, but certainly swimmable. Suitable for body surfing or learning surfers. Regular, fairly small waves.

One of our favourite beaches in all of Sri Lanka!

We then move to Mirissa- 1 1/2 hours in taxi.

review_text:
Having walked down beautiful AdamÂ’s Peak, been mesmerized by the scenery in Ella, soaked in the ambience of Tangalle and Mirissa, Hikkaduwa was not only a huge disappointment, but also felt dreadfully unsafe.

Whilst Tangalle and Mirissa were lined with the flora and fauna of Sri Lanka, there were a few coconut trees in Hikkaduwa, but mostly the view is of delapidated, eery, empty hotels. Unlike elsewhere where you could easily get delicious Sri Lankan food for a good price, this place was full of naff restaurants serving expensive Western food, and poor quality at that. 

Perhaps the most difficult thing is the large groups of local men just wandering around gawking at tourists and in particular hassling women. Having travelled lots of the South for two weeks we expected some people to peddle their wares, but this was constant and at times quite aggressive. At one point whilst I was trying to read my book I had to tell somebody to back away because he was pestering so much. Hardly relaxing.

In terms of the tourist population, whilst in other places it was full of backpackers travelling around, here it was mostly what seemed to be people on package deals just here for the beach. Unfortunately, it did give it quite a chavvy vibe and felt somewhat cheap but not cheerful, and not actually even cheap!

*Perhaps most distressing was the Â‘turtle watchingÂ’* Basically, a group of Sri Lankan guys encourage large sea turtles onto the shore (possibly captured and brought in) and feed them seaweed to keep them close. If tourists were to feed them seaweed they have to pay a fee. I gather if they dont pay they get quite intimidating. These tourists then go up to these beautiful creatures and distress them by petting them and taking pictures with them. It really is heartwrenching to see, and astounding how oblivious so many tourists are to how awful this practice is.

Sri Lanka has so much beauty and excitement to offer - thank goodness I only spent one day here as it doesnÂ’t show you how great Sri Lanka is. I would discourage anyone from visiting this place.

review_text:
Ive been to Hikka a few times now and I love it there. the beaches are lush, real long sandy beaches with a range of surf options from beginner right up to top level. when theres no surf theres a reef right off the main beach where you can see lots of fish and turtles from. the waters real clear here and warm. 
if youre going for nightlife this is the place to be, theres pretty much a party in a different club every night and the parties get loose. particularly over new years and xmas when the parties are massive. 
theres also lots of shops and stuff to have a look at to entertain yourself and theres plenty other things to visit like the turtle conservation place and the elephant orphanage isnt too far away
hikkaduwa is an epic place but is quite busy with a fairly loud main road with traffic most the night

review_text:
IÂ’m not typically a beach person, I find the more popular beaches to be much the same around the world (packed full of overpriced bars/restaurants etc) but there are some amazing things that set this beach apart from the rest. 

We headed down to the beach around 8am with the hope of seeing a wild giant sea turtle feeding and we were lucky enough to find one! This was one of our main hopes for this trip as we love animals. There were a couple of people there already and shortly after there were more and more people but they all seemed to be respectful and gave the turtle space to do as it pleased. There are some officials who Â“policeÂ” the area so they would stop anyone from touching the turtle etc. 

Having been amazed by the turtle we then used our own snorkel in the shallows and it was full of various fish and other marine life , there were plenty of people offering snorkel tours to a close by rock (by boat) which we may do tomorrow. 

We walked up the beach and stopped at a place for some breakfast, it was average but we just needed to eat something. ThereÂ’s plenty of choice for food but IÂ’ve found that the better places are a short walk inland from the seafront. 

We went back to our room to top up our sun cream and headed back to the beach where we had a drink in the shade before renting some body boards and having some fun in the waves! The waves are very strong so I would not let children play in the sea without an accompanying adult!

Although IÂ’m not a fan of beaches in general I found it was rich in marine life which was incredible to see and the body boards were 300 rupees each for an hour which seemed like good value.

review_text:
Came here on the train from Mirissa having heard good things. Instantly disappointed. Outside our hotel, thatÂ’s another review in itself, Coral Sands hotel (a relic of a bygone era with some relics still coming to holiday each year).

Hikkaduwa beach is littered with rubbish and the water in some parts is full of boats so it makes it very difficult to swim. 

The beach front itself is littered with beach bars most of which are terribly overpriced and people constantly try to sell you either clothes or other trinkets when you are trying to relax. 

The atmosphere on the beach is nowhere near as chilled as Mirissa. Another horrific experience was watching people poking and prodding the sea turtles. Leave the bloody things alone!!!

There are plenty of dive resorts and surf schools too but be cautious. I scuba dive in Ireland and looked at two schools, would not go near them. Old tatty BCDs, dirty regulators and old boats. Nah cheers mate!

The surf schools will rent you a board no problem but donÂ’t expect much from them in terms of a surf report, we just got told Â“um yes loads of wavesÂ”. Nothing about reefs, rips of good spots. Also be cautious of local surfers, they have a tendency to drop in on you even if you have caught the wave.

We were told by a surf school Â“no rocks all sandÂ” but my girlfriend was wiped out and hit her foot on a shallow reef. Now I knew about the reef but the guy in the school assured me, Â“not to worry, very deepÂ”. 

Not knowing the topography of the sea I expected the school to inform me having never surfed the area before. 
 
In short if you have been to Mirissa before here or are planning to go to Mirissa before Hikkaduwa then stay away. 

In classic Irish terms Â“this place is a bleedinÂ’ Kip!!!Â”

review_text: Great beach, particularly for surfers although main break attracts beginners who tend to spoil surfing for those who can already surf. There are various areas that are good for learning to surf. Nice sand and restaurants on the beach. Also some very good restaurants on the main road and those off the main road tend to be cheaper and often serve more authentic Sri Lankan food. The beach is not well suited to families with young children as the waves break very close to shore. Fishing village at the eastern end worth walking too. Good location for sightseeing along the coast towards Bentota and to the east to Galle and beyond.

review_text:
Hikkaduwa was a huge disappointment.  

The ocean was very, very rough and we could not even enter the water in some areas.  We visited at the end of July - it is apparently much calmer after December.  The sand is not fine and powdery and there was garbage strewn about.  Peddlers were plentiful but mainly tolerable; it was the random men who hang around the beach who were very annoying.  

Hikkaduwa town is dirty, noisy, and chaotic.  Walking down the 'sidewalk' or crossing the road is downright dangerous - the buses and other vehicles fly by pedestrians and each other at fairly high speeds in tight quarters.  I am surprised there aren't more accidents.  The fumes and pollution from vehicles is overwhelming.  Proprietors are aggressive.  It seems like everyone is trying to get something from you or sell something to you.  It's exhausting.

I am not sure what tourists see in this place - beauty must really be in the eye of the beholder.

review_text:
We fell in love with Sri lanka 2 years ago, and since its only a 4hr flight from Dubai, we go as often as we can. Trying a new beach everytime. Hikkaduwa is bwautifull (not as lovely as Bentota).
During our last trip in Hikkaduwa we were walking along the beach at aroumd 8pm in search of a seafood restaurant. As we walked pass the Hikka Tranz hotel, there was a young lady sitting on the beach. A few metres away from her there was a low hanging tree and I saw this Sri Lankan sitting there, watching her, thinking since it was dark he cant be seen. It was eerie. I walked up to the hotel security that was near thr pools,and informed them.
We found a restaurant on the beach not far from where we saw this guy hide.
Waiting for our food I saw my husband being distracted. A young woman came up from thr beach, looked at the menu and turned back towards the beach to walk back the way she came. My husband jumped up and went to her, spoke to her briefly and she turned back towards the restaurant walking through towards the main rd. Its then that my husbanded pointed out to me a man who was following the girl. When se stopped at the restaurant to view the menu, he walked past just a few steps and stood in the shadows watching her. Luckily my husband was observant and said that he saw them drom a diatance already. 
While he spoke to the lady, he pointed out the man, who was startled and turned his back.
When she walked through the restaurant, he made a dash through the alley way next door to the main road as well. Luckily she got a tuk tuk. I could swear it was the same guy sitting under the bushes at the tree.
I was so shaken by it all.
So ladies, PLEASE be careful. Dont walk alone on the deserted beaches at night. Please.

review_text:
I definitely loved Hikkaduwa beach, I don't know how it is during peak season but I was here in July. There wasn't a lot of people and I loved it. It felt like a clean beach to just stroll in and relax in. It was also a good beach to swim in. 

One side has bigger waves and rocky while the other is sandy.  
 They also have wild turtles swimming here where the locals help you  get seaweed to feed the turtles so it will come to shore. 

I initially saw a crowd of people and asked what was happening. I was curious. I was saddened though that a local approached me and asked for money for me to see the turtle--- they said if i didn't give them money then it wouldn't come to shore. 

I dive anyway, so I just walked away and let it be. However, they do exist in the area. You can see them naturally in knee length deep, of course, the locals are just trying to get money out of you. 

I generally loved my whole trip in Sri Lanka --- it felt safe even when I was alone.  What I got really tired of though is tuktuk drivers over charging tourists. 

In Hikkaduwa, the locals would approach me every so often because most were in groups and I was alone.   Don't get me wrong, I love mingling---I am a people person. I love meeting new people and I like interacting wiht locals but in Hikkaduwa it was a bit much! 

I would laze in the beach andthey would sort of wake me to just strike a lot of conversations, usually sales related.  Often, a group of french people rescued me because they kept asking about my hotel and if I wanted to come over which of course I didn't.  I do love mingling with locals but it just gets a tadbit too muich if  they constantly come when you are lazing and resting. I guess, I was a target since most were in groups or couples and I was alone. 

All else, I still did enjoy Hikkaduwa.

If you are into snorkelling and especially, if you are a nature/animal lover, you will be disappointed by people's behaviour in turtle point which i'll call "circus point". Some locals  are giving algaes to tourist so they can take pictures and videos. So, they end up being 3 or 4 people disturbing 1 or 2 turtles which sometimes can't even swim. 
And the 'funny" part is that the same local guys giving algaes, (for money of course and that is another story...) are asking them not to touch the turtles when feeding them. It's like what they do is not bad, the problem is just when you touch the animal....

 If you just ignore this horror scene and go some meters further for snorkelling, you'll probably end up surrounded by boats with glass bottoms which are taking people who don't swim. So you can't enjoy it since   you have to be careful and to look up and around instead of looking down. So if i gave one out of 5, it's just for the beautiful fish that we couldn't even admire as we wanted.

We were out o season so it was quiet. From the various signs, the Russians have found here. The beach is scenic but plastic debris everywhere. The beach is famous for its turtles. 

A local man sidled up to us keen to show us the turtles. He had a younger companion who entered the sea to entice a turtle to me using seaweed - and it worked - to some extent and I did catch a glimpse of a large turtle close by. 

Of course these gentlemen wanted to be paid for their time and effort and help the local community. A further (persistent)  offer to sample the local Aloe Vera was declined. 

The beach has many watering holes and we enjoyed some calamari and beer at the end of the morning.

review_text:
The coral reef glass boat ride was an ad-hoc proposal by our local guide as a short activity during our Galle-to-Bentota ride. 

June is not the best season for sailing far out to areas of better diversity because of the current but we were able to see quite a good variety of marine life including sea turtle on the shallower reef side. There are a few people snorkelling so you can probably see the same things without paying for the ride. However note the sea can get quite choppy, combine that with shallow waters and rocky bottoms, a boat ride is not a bad option if you are interested to see the reef.

review_text:
Our Hotel had entrances directly onto the beach so we took regular strolls along it as well as swam / snorkelled from it.

It is a public beach (why not), and there are plenty of people around but it is not unpleasantly crowded.and the food / beverage shacks etc add to the ambience.

Yes there are boat vendors etc along the shore, but they generally accept a polite no, and don't hassle you further.

We especially liked the area to the North, where most of the locals went (en masse), to enjoy themselves, and seeing them happy, made us happy too.

Going into the sea from this beach is very easy and no rubber footwear required,

Warning, be vigilant of the many small tourist boats that operate in a most cavalier way in the same area.
I snorkelled out lots of times, wearing bright flourescent gear.
However, I had to stop many times, and shout loudly at the boat crew, to make them aware of my presence.( they were too busy amusing their customers by doing fast 'doughnuts' in the water and throwing bread over for the fish)
This was very unsafe practice and dangerous to swimmers..
The authorities, should segregate the boats from swimmers by roped off areas with marker buoys, as they are in many other parts of the world.

It is also  a great shame to see ignorant people feeding the fish bread etc and feeding / stroking the turtles.too.
Titillating as it may be for you, please stop and think, as you are changing the diet and behaviour of the marine life. Thereby, you are quite literally killing them.
Maybe some informative notices need to go up along the beach ( and make sure they are in written in the Russian language too ).

We still love the place, and would not hesitate to return here at any time.

review_text:
The beach is nice, and within yards you can see lots of tropical fish if you can snorkel. You don't need anyone's help to see the fish, or for them to be fed. So beware of touts offering trips in glass bottom boats and snorkelling assistance. We got conned because it was our first day in SL. The glass boat was rubbish, you cannot see much through the old glass and there are very few fish in the marine sanctuary part anyway. Then we were kitted out with life jackets and snorkelling gear and lead to the shallow part where locals were playing in the water. There were lots of fish here, but there was no reason to pay someone to see this. Better to bring your own snorkel and enjoy.
The rains came and the water became unclear so we did not see the turtles even though we went to the other side of the beach.

The guy who was supposed to act as our paid life guard was sitting bored while my kids were in the water  - they were not in any danger but I realised he had oversold his credentials. 

As others have said, the fish and turtles do not belong to locals, so take your own bread to feed them and avoid the useless operators who are trying to hassle and exploit visitors.

review_text:
We were told the name is "turtle beach" by our Air BNB owner.  We took a tuk tuk in and went to the first part of the beach which had large waves in the afternoon, perfect to jump over, boogie board, and body surf.   If you walk down the beach toward the hotel there is a small stone stairway that leads you to another area of the beach.  It is more coral and is a little rockier, but it also has sea turtles who will swim in throughout the day.   My kids each had a chance to put on a mask and swim along side the gentle creatures.  It was an amazing experience.  One thing, PLEASE DO NOT TOUCH THE TURTLES.  They are wild animals and this can harm them.   There was a wonderful local man who spent his day reminding tourist it is not okay to touch the turtles.  

There were lots of opportunities for snorkeling and diving with a shop on site to rent equipment.  The beach was also clean and quiet - great for reading watching the waves, or taking a nap.  

There are also fruit salesman on the beach.  It sounds  silly, but it was fun to drink from a coconut and eat fresh pineapple on the beach.  We bartered the price down to about 800 rupies - be ready to do that :)

review_text: We first stopped for a short time on a tour, but saw that it had a lot to offer so when we had a free day in Columbo we took the two hour train ride to Hikaduwa. (Don't get suckered in to first class like we did, go second. See my other review) the streets are full of shops, bars, restaurants and some street food. We felt adventurous, so got some bbq fish and chicken from a stall at the beach car park. Wow! It's local, authentic, which means the fish is roughly chopped bbq'd sauced and spiced, as is the chicken and served in a cardboard dish. Lots of meat on the fish. Beautiful. Ask for spicy otherwise it will be mild. On to the beach. All manner of water sports on offer; scuba, snorkelling, glass bottom boat, surfing hire, lessons. We just swam and snorkelled in the warm water. At the southern end of the beach large sea turtles are found while wading in the shallow reef. Not sure why they stay there, they don't seem distressed at all the people's attention. Beautiful to watch up close. Lots of coconut vendors and beachfront restaurants. We had lunch at "Parrots paradise" (see other review). Don't forget to have them open the nut after drinking to scrape the flesh.. yum. We also bought a small bottle of calypso white rum from a bottle shop, well worth it to top up the coconut.  Beach gets really hot in the middle of the day with not much shade around, so maybe a cafe, restaurant or bar. Morning, terrific. Great day was had. ??

There were quite a few surfers and lots of places where you could hire snorkels, a boat trip, scuba lessons, etc. There were also a lot of people selling coconuts, pineapples and items of clothing. If you show the slightest interest in the clothing the ladies are very difficult to say no to if you donÂ’t agree on a price. I witnessed this with a chap who wasnÂ’t happy with the price and the lady was very dogged in her attempt to make a sale. If you say no straight away, they leave you alone. There are a lot of fish very close to the waters edge and some locals feed them and you can see them almost jumping out of the water to get the food. We also saw a turtle very close to the beach and lots of tourists crowding around it and touching it - please do not touch them if you are lucky enough to see one yourselves. 
On a downside, there is a lot of litter around the beach and around Hikkaduwa in general.

review_text:
Jungle beach is rather pleasant once you get there.

Access is via a mountain path that is medium long, rocky and uneven and whilst the agile and fit can negotiate it with ease it is difficult for most of us over 70 - as I am.

There is a nice shack on the beach that serves decent food at reasonable prices.

The water is fresh and clear, the beach nice clean and good sand.

When it came to leave I was told that the easiest route was to walk along the sea path back to Unawatuna. I was also told it would take me 5-10 min.

How wrong was this info. I am sure a mountain goat could have negotiated the uneven and loose boulders far better than my arthritic sloth like agility, the boulders are rather hazardous but eventually you come to another beach. Then you have to climb back up the mountain !!

Bad choice should have gone up the way I went down.

That said, it looks to be an enclosed and small beach, so may be great for families or those looking to escape the tourists.

This is a delightful beach in its own little cove.  It is nicely sheltered and offers reasonably good snorkelling very close-by the shore.  The fact that you have to walk a bit to get here is a big plus.

We came two days before Independence day, which was a Saturday, so it was probably one of the busiest days, which meant it was overcrowded.  There was also a disappointing amount of litter.

I feel that if you came mid-week and it was not a major national holiday, this place would be really special.

review_text:
I had only heard great things about jungle beach so decided it was definitely worth a visit.

I walked there from Unawatuna and was glad I'd read reviews on here describing how to get there because it is not really signposted until you are almost there. 

I enjoyed the walk and locals were helpful in pointing me in the right direction. Don't expect an easy stroll - it is quite a trek on uneven and narrow trails with large rocks. However, you may be lucky to see monitor lizards, peacocks and other animals along the way like I did. 

When I got to the beach I was quite disappointed - maybe it was the time of year but the water was rough and dirty, the sands were littered with rubbish and debris. My belief that I could snorkel in tranquil waters and see lots of beautiful fish was instantly killed. In the 5 mins I tried to go into the water, I got scratched quite badly by rocks you cannot see through the murky waters.  Even when I tried to go into the water further up the beach, I quickly got out again due to the amount of rubbish wrapping itself around my legs. Such a shame - but I bet the waters are calmer, clearer and the beach cleaner at high season in Summer.

At least I saw a huge monitor lizard - that was really cool.

review_text:
Jungle Beach is really a short walk from Unawatuna (about 40-60 min) through the jungle then climb down to the beach that is secluded and overlooks Galle.

First came here over 3 years ago and it felt more exciting back then as it really was like a trek in the jungle but this time, felt that Unawatuna in general and the walk to Jungle Beach was now becoming more built up and busy. The walk passes through dozens and dozens of hotels and B&B's and it is likely to be more crowded and busy once the monstrosity of a hotel is built in the Unawatuna beach! So better get here quick before it loses its charm.
The positives is that because the area still belongs to the Dept of Wildlife, they have stopped or done away with the previous make-shift restaurants that were right by the beach at Jungle Beach.
It seems to be more of a place where a lot of locals come in for a day/weekend trip. Since we went there on a Sunday, it was very busy. Also a tad noisy but everyone seemed to be having a good time. 
You can swim here too but the sea is now seems to be littered.
Strangely though the walk from Unawatuna and though the jungle seemed clean and came across only a few discarded PET bottles.
The climb is only slightly difficult but recommend shoes unless you are a flip-flop pro in which case you can still easily do the climb up and down unless you are unlucky to do the trek on a rainy day.
Make sure to take lots of water though, as it is humid.
There are a few restaurants around in the vicinity before you climb down to the beach that offers local food for good prices. We didn't have lunch there, so no idea how the food was.
If you don't fancy eating after the walk, you can always a grab a bite to eat once you get to Dalewala road which has all the touristy shops/restaurants.

review_text:
I've visited Sri Lanka three times over the recent years and always make a visit to jungle beach. This time I was shocked and saddened to see how much rubbish and plastic were left on the beach. The locals who work at the beach bar must do something urgently to prevent these plastic bottles and other items from entering the water. 

I've added photos to show the rubbish tip on jungle beach. This tip was found at the far side of the beach, opposite the beach bar and sun lounges.

Furthermore the swimming experience at jungle beach was awful. I stepped on and swam through heaps of plastic bags. The worst part is that I spied a small turtle swimming through this too.

Unfortunately it's been raining and storming a lot in galle over past days so plastic from the beach is no doubt being pushed and blown into the waters. Me and my boyfriend tried to take as much rubbish as we could back up with us but there's still tons down there. The locals and tourists who enjoy this beach must be more waste aware and not dispose of their rubbish so carelessly.

I would like to add photos however the file sizes are too large and trip advisor only allows 5mb photo uploads.

There were lots of high rising waves but no dangerous currents . 
Not rocky either so was safe in the sense that you didnÂ’t need to worry about hitting against the rocks . 
Since we visited soon after tourism was recovering  post covid lockdown , it wasnÂ’t crowded . 
Lots of food shacks  right on the beach . Beach parties for the party lovers at night . 
One of the main activities around ,other than surfing is whale watching and a must try if you are in Mirissa. 
To reach here , itÂ’s a two and a half hour drive from the airport , through the beautiful highway . 
Would surely suggest that you plan a day or two stay around Mirissa bay if  you are visiting Sri Lanka.

A beautiful stretch of beach with some quite strong waves. Perfect for a romantic stroll at sunset and having a bite to eat in one of the many beach restaurants.  

However beautiful this beach is during the day, in the evening  the techno-terror starts. From early evening until early morning the beach is covered by the bum-bum and electronic drums of the local techno-beach club. The basses are hamming through every wall.

What a pity. One single dance club destroying this previously pristine location with its noise.

Sad to say that I will not return anymore.

review_text:
Mirissa Beach is located just 20 minutes away from Matara by bus, making it easily accessible for tourists and locals alike. The beach is known for its stunning scenery, crystal-clear waters, and pristine sands, making it the perfect spot for swimming and relaxing under the sun.

One of the highlights of Mirissa Beach is its cozy bars and restaurants, which offer a variety of delicious food and drinks for visitors to enjoy. Whether you're looking for a refreshing cocktail or a delicious seafood dinner, you'll find plenty of options here.

review_text:
Just returned from Sri lanka, where we stayed for 3 nights in Mirissa beach. We had stayed in Unawatuna on a previous visit, so wanted to try a different beach this time. Having spent 7 days on the east coast, which was off season, Mirissa was nearing the end of peak season and much livilier. 
We wanted a place on the beach side of the road, so choose Sea World hotel, which had fantastic views and excellent breakfast. We didnt book evening meals, because the daily blackouts meant that we had to choose places with a generator. The blackouts during the day didnt bother us, as we spent most of this time travelling around to different beaches and places. Cold beers and food was always available somewhere.
The beach bars and restaurants on Mirissa beach were mostly all open day and evening, and even when the blackouts came there were plenty of candles making it even more romantic.
I had heard the road along Mirissa beach was very busy and no footpaths and I would have to say it was really dangerous when we were there, especially at night when there was no street lighting. It really was a challenge to avoid speeding tuk tuks and buses.
If I was to compare Mirissa to Unawatuna I would say that Unawatuna is at the end of a small road far from the main road, so much safer to walk around the main street and go in and out of bars shops etc

review_text:
We visited Mirissa for 10 days and visited 4 beaches, ate at several restaurants, swam with wild seat turtles, watched baby turtles hatching (by shear luck and coincidence) surfed, was taught yoga, had massages and met lovely people.
The beaches we visited were all beautiful to look at as you might expect. The main beach to the west was the largest and were we spotted the turtles. Perfect for lazy days and strolling along rather than using the road that runs parallel. It has an abundance of restaurants all selling fish (some fresher than others). At night is is quite noisy with every restaurant and bar trying to out do the other with trance/ dance music which kind of ruined the atmosphere for us a little. The smaller bays to the east are far more relaxed and just as beautiful with some lovely bars and hammocks. The music can still turn a little hectic but you can still find some chilled spots to drink and hang out. 
There are some scenic spots to check out (perfect for intsergrammers) but if you like to go to them to see the beauty for what it is rather than take a picture of yourself in a Â“just stumbled across me like this poseÂ” it can be a little annoying as they are everywhere! 
On the whole its a great place to base yourself and check out the south coast of Sri Lanka.  
Turtle Bar was one of our favourites to hang out at. The staff are super friendly and the food was the best of all the restaurants we ate at.

review_text:
After two weeks in Sri Lanka, this was by far the worst place I have eaten. 

Opted for catch of the day seafood, big mistake. Firstly, the prices were extortionate. Once we had ordered we were disregarded, as finding new people to rip off was more important than serving existing customers. I had to take my teapot to the bar for a refill despite the 10% service charge......? 

When my two jumbo prawns finally arrived, one was completely mushy & black. The meal was served with cold dry rice (supposed to be chips). When being charged 2000 R, I expected much better. 

After resistance, It was agreed that I wouldnÂ’t be charged for the inedible prawn but it was still added to the bill as one last attempt to catch us out. The manager had no interest in customer service and just laughed at us. 

Avoid at all costs, there are much better places. Dishonest & disgusting.

review_text:
Stopped at Mirissa on our way to Colombo from the south. The town is charming and the open beach spots are spectacular. A wonderful blend of people of all ages swimming, walking down the beach, eating what seems to be super great sea food, surfing, bathing in the sun, having refreshments. The spots serving food/drinks are peppered throughout and you can simply setup on the beach or stay at one of them. Simple and easy yet an experience not to miss.
Wish I could surf!

We visited during the day in December, we arrived at around 9am with two children under 4.

We found a nice area to sit as part of a bar / restaurant, there is no charge to use the seats as long as you use the bar for drinks.

We had fresh coconuts (priced around Â£1 each) and some nice food.

The sea is calm compared to some of the coast, so perfect for children.  The beach is not as busy as others along the coast, and shops etc near by if needed.

It is a sand only beach which is perfect for the kids.

review_text:
My husband and I have just spent four days at the northern end of Marisa Beach in a hotel called Number One Marisa. (See my review RE this hotel.)

The surf has been constant during our stay here and my husband has averaged two surfs a day, early morning and early evening.

There is a main road of simple shops; a supermarket, atm, wine store and a few handicraft shops. 

Along the beach are several restaurants, and of an evening the beach comes to life with seafood restaurants. Boats and carts stacked with ice and displaying todayÂ’s catch ...prawns, lobsters, fish, calamari etc. Just select what you want to eat and they cook it for you. Most of them offer happy hour beverages.

At the south end of the bay is an island that is accessible at low tide... challenging but a great vantage point. 

Tips: 
Rock shoes for the coral bottom when surfing. 
Be patient with the language - Sri LankanÂ’s are very happy people and try hard to please. 
Tip$$$ ....as their wages are quite minimal and hours of work long.

review_text: For the four days we spent in Mirissa, we chose the same spot, next to the lifeguard tower, in front of a turtle egg nursery, and in the shade of some low trees. It was a perfect place to enjoy the beach. The waves can sometimes be big and me and my pre-teen daughter had great fun diving under them as they broke over our heads. But smaller children should stick to paddling in the shallows. There were no hawkers hassling us to buy drinks or trinkets, and the three small stray dogs, whose patch seemed to include that part of the beach, paid us no attention and didn't bother us at all. At night, the beach bars are lit up and are a great place to chill out after a hot day. Note: I didn't see any showers at the beach, so to freshen up, you'll have to go back to your accommodation.

review_text:
Tragically on Mon 15 Apr at 2:40pm there was a drowning incident at this beach. The waves were extremely strong, further compromising the normal conditions which feature a strong tidal rip.

Assisting with the rescue were two doctors, a nurse, a paramedic and a firefighter. All foreigners. It took ten minutes for local lifesavers to arrive on scene even though they were less than 200m down the beach. Once there the lifesavers stood back and observed without relieving tiring people whom were performing CPR or offering any direction or reassurance that further assistance was on the way. 

The CPR balloon and defibrillator on site did not function. After we loaded the individual in the ambulance it took a further three minutes for the driver to turn the vehicle around and get it moving towards the hospital.

After the ambulance had departed witnesses sought out lifeguards to give a statement; they seemed surprised at this and there was no template for an incident report or recording our details. During discussion one of the lifeguards indicated Â“today was a bad day to go in the waterÂ” but shrugged when asked why people were not being discouraged. 

I would strongly caution against young children or inexperienced swimmers entering the water here. I hope the individual and his family are okay and I offer my thanks and respect to those people that did what they could to assist.

review_text:
Mirissa Beach is beautiful.  We love swimming in the ocean and this place did not disappoint. The water was crystal clear and warm. There was a few big waves which may be challenging for inexperienced swimmers but I would recommend they swim in the patrolled section in the middle of the beach.

The southern end of the beach near Parrot Rock is great for snorkelling as well as a shallow pool for little kids to swim. There are plenty of bars and restaurants along the stretch of the beach if you would like a bite to eat or something to drink.

review_text: Mirissa Beach is up there with the best beaches along the south coast. It has a multitude of restaurants and bars overlooking the water. It's a very well-known spot for surfers as the water is fit for both beginners and more experienced surfers alike. It's very easy to get to and there are a ton of hotel accommodations nearby should you plan to stay in the area. Tuk tuks flood the streets throughout the day making it easy to just swing by, or stay the whole day. It's also one of the more lively, party-like spots of the South Coast.

review_text: If you want to swim with big turtles search the small beach named Coconut bay just under the Coconut Tree Hill also named Coconut Garden. For a very small price you can rent snorkeling equipment from a nice guy named Sandaru. No other taxes are requested. You cand find him on the beach at Turtle Point. I attached picture with him. We rented flippers from him for around 200 LKR/ person as we had snorkeling masks. He will show you the best place to search and swim with the turtles. We went two times there. In the first day we saw one big turtle and in the second day in the morning we saw 4 turtles out of which one was extremly big. We higly recommand to spend few hours on this beach. Also, on the hill you can take very nice pictures.

review_text:
Stunning beach with to die for sunrises and sunsets. It gets very busy at night, but what a fabulous atmosphere to soak up the warm tropical air!
A beautiful walk along the front will take you past the many restaurants and diners, and sun beds are readily available and free! 
The service at restaurants can vary from incredibly poor to very good, depending on which one you choose, the busier ones are often poor service and waiters can just ignore you completely, so if you do stop for a drink, don't wait for them to come to you! 
Prices are more expensive on the beach and can be unreasonable if you've got poor service. Beware of the surf during the day, it gets very high and very strong, small children would need supervising and even string swimmers need to be cautious! 
A must visit when in mirrissa!

I was glad we weren't staying on the beach as it might be noisy at night. 
It is a shame they have ruined the beach with too many buildings. 
This is not an upmarket place: its good for families, backpackers and those who dont mind it being a bit low at heel.

review_text:
We really enjoyed Mirissa Beach. ItÂ’s not too long from end to end, itÂ’s not too crowded, and each bar/hotel that joins the beach to the main road isnÂ’t too expensive. 

The west side is quieter and is best for surfing.

The middle has the most parasols and is the best for swimming.

The east side has a little island to walk to and get great views. This side is the nosiest (closest to the road) and is the best for party bars.

In summary - itÂ’s not expensive to eat and drink from breakfast to dinner, itÂ’s safe for kids and pensioners, itÂ’s clean, itÂ’s not overcrowded, the sand is very soft.... what more could you ask for!

review_text:
The beach is very nice and clean, the water was very warm (around 28 degrees) and also clean and there were some nice big waves sometimes (that's if you are into big waves). 
But be aware that it can get very crowded sometimes. We were in February 2019 and until 10 am you had to occupy a sun bed, otherwise they was nothing free anymore until around 4 pm (or you had to be lucky). 

One thing which i didn't like: all the restaurants (to whom the sunbeds belonged) were telling you at around 4:30 pm-5 pm to get off the sunbeds, because they were replacing them with tables for dinners. I found that they did this much too early ! It was exactly the time when the sun wasn't that strong anymore and it was really nice to lie in the sun and you had to go. I know that it gets dark really fast there, but still , I wish they had begun with this at 6 pm or later. 
The area around the beach is not nice though. There is a LOT of garbage lying around  everywhere and stinking (especially in the small river, yuck), there is a lot of dust and a lot of noise from the traffic on the main street and also no sidewalk, so you had to pay a lot of attention to the cars coming from both sides. So not really a place to walk relaxed in the evening.
The service on the beach is terrible (with a few exceptions). Very slow waiters, you had to wait a lot for everything (menu, drinks, food, even the bill), they forget a lot from the orders and for some of them there is 10% percent service charge already included ( a service which is as I said terrible). But the service and the food is generally much better on the main street than on the beach (we found some places with really amazing food and very good service). 
So 4 stars for the beach itself, which is very beautiful, but not for the area surrounding the beach or the service on the beach.

At first I can't decide whether to choose Mirissa or Unawatuna. These 2 beaches is just nearby and u can just go to one place to another by bus. Personally I like Unawatuna more than Mirissa.

Mirissa is very popular with Whale Watching. You can ask the price around and I can say most of the boat companies / agents selling the ticket for LKR3000 (discounted price). The difference is only, which agent can give you opportunity to sit at the top deck and also at the front row. 

I bought a whale watching ticket from Panorama Guesthouse Mirissa with a tagline "money back guarantee" if you don't see a whale. 

Unfortunately I can't even see a whale on that day and didn't get my refund. So, my advice..don't worry much about the seating places on the boat, there is no promises when u dealing with nature, animals, etc. 

If you have a short time in Mirissa, just enjoy the beach and skip whale watching.

review_text:
Before we set of for our adventure in Sri Lanka I was torn between staying in Unawatuna or Mirissa so we decided to stay a couple of days in each. Me and my partner visited Mirissa for 3 days and was slightly disappointed. We found that the beach was busy and didnÂ’t look anything like the pictures advertised. The beach is big and wide but I prefer smaller beach with more of a tropical feel to it. DonÂ’t get me wrong if your into surfing itÂ’s great but not so great for a relaxing swim.
We also found that the main Road was busy, dusty, smelly with lots of litter. If your looking for somewhere thatÂ’s calmer and cleaner I would look elsewhere on the south coast. We did do the whale watching in Mirissa which was great! This was with the whale watching club who I would highly recommend. We also stayed in Unawatuna prior to Mirissa. Unawatuna Beach was just ok but a 5 minute tuk tuk away was Wijaya Beach which was heavenly!  Long and narrow and lined with palm trees. It was also very clean! You can also watch a beautiful sunset here.

review_text:
We had a trip of 3days to cover downsouth. First stop was Mirissa Beach & Parrot Rock. You can easily access to the Mirissa beach from the main road and the Parrot rock is visible from miles. Through the beach you can reach Parrot rock. It is a small island separated from the main land and you can have a mesmerizing 360Â° view of the sea when you climb up. 

You can swim in the Mirissa Main beach as well as the best place I found is the small beach situated on the right side of the Parrot rock. there the water is shallow for a long distance. But when you go further there will be rocks under water and you have to be careful of it.  Waves are not very tide. Can enjoy a good evening swim there. Children also can enjoy a good swim there. 

There are some local restaurants by the beach. We did not go there so not sure about the food & beverages they have and the prices. The beach will be lightly crowded in the evening. But the best time to visit also is the evening, around 3-4. 

After a 1-2hr bath we went to have a hot tea and to eat something. We found this small place called "Spice Rotti shop" by the main road. It is on google map. the food was amazing and prices also very affordable. They have a variety of sri lankan foods and in there we met some foreign travellers also. They customize your food up to your taste. If you are around Mirissa prefer to try this place. 

Don't choose the rainy season to visit Mirissa, as the waves will be rough. Mirissa beach is a Must visit if you are a beach lover.

review_text:
We're in Mirissa for the final week of our trip and I've been stressing for ages about finding turtles and what beach you can see them near here. Google searches suggested we needed to go near Galle to see them, which was disappointing.

But then we were recommended by our villa's manager to check out Polhena beach. We did a little research. Its 6 or 7 min tuk tuk ride towards Matara. We hired Nirosh as our guide after reading some good reviews. 

It was phenomenal!! Within 10 min we were hanging with turtles. The bay is shallow because of the coral and the waves are far calmer than Mirissa. Nirosh is absolutely sound guy and made the whole thing seem so easy.

If you're in the area, its a definite must! You can find him at the Polhena Bay Resort or call him on 077 5481252.
 
Peter

Absolutely beautiful beach, but you need to be careful. Quite dangerous waves. I, perhaps through not being careful enough entering the water got caught by a wave, thrown over and smashed my head on the sea bed. Was pretty nasty, and could easily have been even worse than the bumps, bruises and cuts I ended up with. 

It is absolutely spectacular, and I don't suggest missing it, just be careful. Particularly with kids. If it can throw a grown man around like a rag doll, then you can work out the rest...

This notwithstanding, hundreds of people were swimming and surfing, so it's obviously possible to do with care.

Had a great time staying at Marissa we stayed across the main road at the southern end of the beach at The Spice Garden and walked the beach each day before breakfast then came back to swim in the beautiful warm water.

We hired snorkels mask and flippers from Sandru up near the Sea Star hotel and swam gently with Turtles amazing experience and worth doing.  Sandru is most accommodating and trust worthy he even took one family out while I minded the gear.

I arrived in Negombo around 9am, as it was too early to check in to my hotel I dumped my bag and headed to the beach to explore. 

From the moment I set foot onto the beach I was continuously hounded by numerous locals, each trying to sell me something - either a boat trip, or various wares they were trying to flog. 

I just wanted to be left alone, explore, feel the sun on my skin, and enjoy the views. But I didnÂ’t get one minutes peace. After about half an hour IÂ’d had enough and left the beach. 

Yes, theyÂ’re relatively friendly, but itÂ’s just damn annoying! When one of them is talking to you, you can see about four or five other vendors circling, waiting for them to leave, so they can then pounce. Not a good experience, unfortunately.

Writing in early March 2022 the main issue is power cuts. I have travelled all over SL in the last 2 months, from Jaffna to Tangalle and the only place I have stayed with long daily power cuts is Negombo. Fine if you're in one of the characterless hotels like Jetwings etc. with their noisey diesel generators. But no fun for the majority staying at smaller more environmentally friendly hotels and guest houses.
And the beach is filthy. 
This is the town most tourists visit on the way in and out of the country. Not a good impression.

review_text:
A beautiful stretch of beach several miles long completely ruined by the amount of rubbish strewn across the whole length of it.

Plastic of all descriptions from tooth brushes to old toys, and of course many many plastic bottles.  Also glass bottles whole and smashed,  as well as other detritus.  Yet worse than this from the wild life perspective is the bits of old fish nets and lines scattered all over the place. A real danger to all forms of marine life.

Feral dogs run loose and defecate everywhere,  worse still my wife witnessed a local also defecating on the edge of the water.

A half-hearted attempt is made to clean the beach by use of a tractor and sand scoop but does not cover even half the beach leaving most of the beach untouched. Saw one so called recycling bin that was used as a general rubbish bin, apart from that there appears no attempt to recycle any of this mess.  

At one point a stream runs across the beach then out to sea that smells strongly of sweage . There is also a small pond that also smells the same.

All the beach bars  and hotels that front onto this stretch of sand serve all their drinks with plastic straws and there are thousands of them every where you look on what should be a lovely natural space.

So if you do walk on this beach keep your saddles on

Negombo Beach is actually quite long.  Our first encounter was on a Sunday near the Jetwing Hotel as the sun was setting.  We saw local families packing up, preparing to head home.  Groups of young men playing beach volleyball and others kicking a soccer ball around.  A few female vendors approached us but we said "no thank you" and they left us alone. 

Two weeks later, we walked to the beach in the morning near the Heritance Hotel and were immediately barraged by people offering tours, boat rides, and souvenirs.  We had wanted to take a nice quiet stroll by the water but left after 10 minutes because it got unbearably annoying because the vendors kept following us. review_text: We arrived into Colombo area for our departure flight back home and had some time to kill so we headed to Negombo (hearing it was a nice way to relax before leaving Sri Lanka). The beaches were full of litter and were no where as pristine as some of the other beaches we visited. There are very expensive restaurants (relative to what we had paid for 2 weeks during out travels around Sri Lanka) that line the beach which are really your only options for food. Overall it was a good way to kill time before we had to depart for our 11pm flight but if you can avoid it with other more interesting activities would recommend skipping.

This beach is only average if you look at it purely for a beach holiday (sun bathing, swimming...). Also when we visited in August the waves were much too big too swim. But, it's stil a really nice beach to take a long beach stroll.

What really shouldn't be missed is the Negombo Beach Park (type it in in Google Maps for the location). All the local families go here to relax, fly their kites, and have fun. It's filled with food vendors and stalls and so on. The ambiance is just great.

We had agreed on a price and paid for a trip to Hikkaduwa, Mirissa and Udawalawe and certain activities there and then the morning of our departure the driver took us to his boss who wanted more money. We refused as it was not what we had agreed on and after a discussion he said "Fine" and we set off. When we were in Mirissa he called the driver and said that we would have to pay for something that he had said would be included. What could we do when we were already there? Avoid this company!

No sun loungers and limited beach bars/restaurant but lots of places on the road side. We chose here rather than finishing in Colombo for the end of our holiday

Beaches in Colombo and Bentota are a lot cleaner!

review_text:
In the summer of 2018 we (Dutch familie of 4, kids 13 and 18) travelled to discover the beauties of Sri Lanka.
Don't expect a wide beach to relax and sunbathe in August: the wind blows fiercely towards the land and the waves are huge!
But we liked jumping in the big waves: we did it every day. It's not for the young, because the undercurrents are very stron and the waves unpredictable. We also recommend to use waterproof sunscreen, because without you noticing it and being all the time with the most part of your body under the cooling water, you will easily get sunburned.

I guess if you have an island with a population of 23 million, and a large chunk of that population is living around Colombo/Negombo, the chance of a pristine beach is almost nil. There was a large swell in the ocean which made swimming unsafe while we were there, plus a large amount of rubbish was washing up, so IÂ’m not sure how safe the swimming would be. 
But itÂ’s still an enjoyable walk. Small beach food stalls are there with good street food, and the locals poured down to fly kites and dip themselves in the water. There are way better beaches in Sri Lanka ( Mirissa comes to mind ), but itÂ’s a good intro into the beach culture in this area.

review_text:
Unlike many reviews on here, our experience was of a very clean beachfront.

Potentially this could be down to what side of the beach you are, but we stayed at the Jetwing Beach hotel and the beach just off the hotel was lovely and clean. 

It was also very quiet which we liked as it gave us time to walk along the beach in peace.

There was some sort of beach gathering further down which we went to see with fun fair rides and stalls which was also lovely to see but I am glad our area was a bit further away so not to have too many people there.

The water is very choppy and rough so we couldn't go into the water but luckily this wasn't our aim so it didn't really impact our day.

I would recommend a stroll along this beach but worth noting that the water is rough and not the most blue.

review_text:
Negombo beach gets a lot of unfair comparisons to the other beaches along the west coast of the island. I heard a lot of complaints about pollution and cleanliness. However, I was pleasantly surprised at the condition of the beach - clean, long empty beaches right at the door step of the hotels.

I said empty above but this was in reference to actual beach goers... If you're brave enough to risk a venture onto the beach you will be hounded by local sellers within seconds. In my experience they don't take no for an answer and they come in their droves to prey on anyone foolish enough to dander onto the beach.

The beach could be good but you won't have time to actually enjoy it unfortunately.

review_text:
Beautiful hotel, I had a sea view cottage and was made so welcome here the food is amazing and you are so well looked after. The manager is always at breakfast greeting you and always checking if all is good with you in the evening, long hours! Everyone was super  friendly, they have an amazing pool, the beach is perfection and the Hotel is very well maintained, because it is well run. All the grounds are maintained and picture perfect.

Nilaveli Crab dinner at the beach bar was sublime.

They have a shuttle bus that got me safely back to the international airport at a good price, thank you.

You can book diving, I think they are about to in house a dive school which would be even better.

review_text:
This is a long beach some 8km long. Roughly in the middle there is a little grid of roads that stretch from the main road to the beach, with a number of restaurants and guesthouses. Most Sri Lankan visitors swim here and there is a 400m or so clean stretch of sand with lifeguards. South (towards Trinco) of this stretch there is a bit of plastic litter on the beach.This worsens after about 1km to the extent that you wouldn't want to walk further let alone swim. You can't directly walk North along the beach as there is a naval training facility. Beyond that there is a short decent stretch of sand in front of a couple of smart hotels (there is also a ticket booth for Pigeon Island here.) Further North the beach is pretty filthy. I would guess things would be better in-season as more hotels would make more of an effort and, I'm guessing, the prevailing winds might be from a better direction.

All along the beach the shore shelves in gently so its shallow a long way out and the waves aren't too big.

review_text: We visited the beach before breakfast each morning and had it to ourselves, we also visited around 5pm each afternoon when it was still quite busy but most visitors were in the shallow water close to shore so it was pretty easy to enjoy a bit of swimming further out and body-surf the occasional wave. There seemed to be a bit of voluntary segregation between the foreign visitors in skimpy bathers and the Sri Lankan day-trippers who were mostly fully clothed even while swimming, but there was no unpleasantness around this and some Sri Lankans in lycra bathers (and some who were fully-clothed) were swimming in the same area as the foreign visitors at the northern end of the beach. There was a surf life-saver patrolled area further south beyond the Pigeon Island boat launching area, that section of the beach and further south was very busy.

review_text:
If you made it to Sri Lanka it's worth considering coming here for 4-5 days beach time rather than the more advanced south... it's quite developed but do not expect much. Nethertheless you can find all a happy tourist needs: local excellent quality seafood, reasonably priced hotels (never pay > $50 per double room here, anything above is a tourist trap) and amazing sunrises on the beach + scuba diving, snorkeling, fishing or dolphins watching trips...
The only dissapointing thing was trash on the beach and lots of stray dogs. Would have been an amazing place without these 2!

review_text:
Nilaveli is a very beautiful beach to walk along. We took a long walk when we stayed at Nilaveli Beach Resort toward the Nilaveli Beach Hotel. In between these two hotels, there were 3-4 little guest houses too. The beachfront belonging to these two hotels and the guesthouses was very clean. These beach areas were marked by a red flag. In between however, there was a lot of garbage on the beach. It looked like some people dumped their big black-plastic-bags-full of garbage on the beach. It was unfortunate that they could not find an alternative to this.

In front of our hotel, the beach was super clean. 

We even saw some beach patrol by armed military closer to the Nilaveli Beach Hotel.

Another interesting factor was seeing a lot of cows on the beach. In the evening they went back to their abode (wherever that might be) in small groups.

review_text: This beach is really perfect, with clean golden sand, backed by palmtrees and screwpines.  My hotel was only 2mins away, so I was very pleased to see there was a lifeguard area just 100m down the beach.  As it was the monsoon season, there were very few visitors, except at weekends when crowds of Sri Lankans arrived in buses to spend the day, bathing and partying, which was a lot of fun as everyone was so friendly.  There's a little lane of shops and cafes behind the beach where everyone gathered to buy toys, sweets and street food,  though it was closed during the week due to lack of visitors.  Most people stay in the lifeguard area, but I enjoy beach walks, so several times I walked a few kilometres southwards, and had it all to myself.  During the monsoon season the sea can be very rough, so it's almost impossible to swim as the current is so dangerous.  Most of the local visitors just stood in the water, in all their clothes!  I expect the beach would be totally different in the tourist season, probably with sunbeds etc., but I liked it as it was, wild and wonderful!

review_text:
Golden sand, wonderful blue Indian Ocean, calm shallow water with small waves, palm trees, boats.
Hardly anyone around, very quiet, one of the last crowd free beaches in Sri Lanka Ã¼ though I guess not for long as new and large hotels now being built.
Apart from enjoying the sunshine, the sea and the view  there is not much else to do, but this was exactly what I was looking for. There are funny dog families on the beach who like to spend their time with human company but they are not hungry beggars at all. They have a unique society and it is fun to observe.
Once in a while cows passing by, trying to chew everything they find, including shoes, but easy to scare them away :) 
I am sure for those who like the active kind of holiday these beaches are not the best but for those who seek for tranquillity and the tropic beaches at the same time this is a very good choice.

review_text:
Nilaveli Beach is a really nice long white sand beach. There are a lot of hotels in Nilaveli and they keep the beach nice and clean. This beach is ideal for swimming, even with little kids (still keep them in your sight). 

Just take a long walk and see local fisherman trying to catch fish. Or sit down, relax and enjoy a cocktail. There are some nice spots where you can sit, drink and eat (owned by the hotels).

Looking at the sea you will notice a small island, this is the famous Pigeon Island (National Park). You can go by boat to this island and do some great snorkelling.

Nilaveli beach is for sure one of the best beaches to swim in Sri Lanka!

Coming form a landlocked country, visiting a beach whenever we travel is a big deal for us. But most of the time, we are dispppointed when we see unclean beaches with stuff discarded by beach goers. Nilaveli was different. The beach was suprisingly clean. I could see why the beach was called Nilaveli - i loved the blue sand and the clean water. Though I didn't venture out of swim, I stood in the water for almost an hour enjoying the feel of clean water against the sand. 

The beach is relatively less crowded on a weekday and filled with locals. I can spend an entire day here, enjoying the sand and the water.

The beach is a long strap sand with some trees. The water is nice without being exceptional. It is not as clear as some Thai beaches.

There are very beautiful hotels on and around the beach. I was there during the high season (August) and I have been surprised by the price. Impossible to find any room for less than 80 US$! 

There are beautiful hotels, like the Nilaveli beach Hotel, where is wonderful to spend the day. Bit at this season it was full booked and I guess a room would cost more than 200 US$. So if you watch your budget, don't go there during high season!

review_text:
remote & relaxing area in Sri Lanka, quiet surroundings, only nature around, few tourists in the whole Nilaveli, almost not seen.

Road from Colombo airport may be not very convenient, 6-8 hours by car, so take the driver or just stay somewhere in the middle for a night.

Trincomalee region is noth east coast, and that is far place to visit the whole country staying only there. I advise that to stay for relax after hiking or after visiting the south. However one day trips to Sigiriya, Dambulla or Wilpattu national park are possible if you hire the car or the driver with the car. That costs, but it is worth it, if you have a limited amount of days in Sri Lanka. 

if you are looking for the tourist facilities, a lot of shops and bars that is not the place for you. That is for the nature lovers and those you prefer to meet the real local culture and try origin local food.

Wide, clean & quiet beach No beach sellers, no dogs, no fishermen, no cafe or restaurant .....only a small herd of cows roam the beach  which suited me fine with on interruptions. Sunrise is stunning if you can get up early enough but well worth it.
View over to Pigeon Island where you can snorkel or dive, boat trip of approx 10 mins you need a ticket for the island and of course pay the boatman. Again no shops or cafe on the island - wonderful, take your own water etc.,  Nilaveli Beach is heaven.

The light in the evenings is beautiful.

review_text:
We went in off season I. E. February however the beach is nothing amazing.  Only average swell, nice blue water but a little misty. Beach itself is wonderfully long but there are spots where there is a lot of plastic around. And there is very little shade

Good family beach but can have big rips.

For us the south and west had nicer beaches this time of year.

Also if you come in off season there is little food or amenities around. This was actually quite nice, just a few local boats going out to pigeon island, but come prepared with supplies.

review_text:
You don't have to be a dedicated gardener to enjoy these gardens. Trees are labelled according to whether they're native, imports, even poisonous- so don't lick these ones!
We had our guide with us, and he had a lot of knowledge about some of the plants and trees, that we may have missed if we'd been by ourselves.
The mahogany trees are spectacular- the root system is about a metre high. The Cannonball tree looks like it has coconuts, but they weigh about 4kg. The palm trees lining one path are huge, and the little ones in between them are the same type, but look different when they're younger.
We saw flying foxes, a water monitor, birdlife, and there's an orchid house, and a small suspension bridge.
We were here a few hours, and it was a very pleasant visit. Well recommended.

review_text:
This centuries old botanical garden planned by the British in the centre of the hill station Kandy, Sri Lanka is huge.

There are a number of covered exhibits category wise like seasonal flowers, cactus, perennial et al.,
The place is well maintained and the pathways are clean.

A number of families picnicking in the park are also mindful of the trash they generate and are meticulous in keeping the area clean.

There are a number of species of plants and trees which are imported from across the world and are thriving in the botanical garden.

One needs atleast a couple of hours to walk around the garden and enjoy the nature.

The entry fee to the garden is reasonable and the park is secured fully by barbed wire fencing.

The security checks at the entrance are robust.

 Take your camera along.

Recommended.

review_text: This is a massive garden that is well-maintained with more than 4,000 species of plants, range from humongous trees to herbs, flora, palm trees, orchids, etc. It was built since 14th century as royal  garden, but was destroyed during British occupation and was made as garden for coffee and cinnamons in 19th century. It was then under the administration of Department of Agriculture since 1912 when it was established. Beautiful place to spend for half a day especially for plants lovers. Many sitting benches, people also doing picnic on the lawns. Toilets are available within the park. Many different sections, such as palm tree sections, giant trees, orchid garden, cacti section, flowerbed section, etc. There is a section with interesting sights of lots of visible hanging bats on the tree branches. Overall it was a pleasant and therapeutic session to walk around the garden. Brochure indicates various species of birds can be found in the garden, but we could hardly see any. Also, the entrance fee is rather steep for foreigners at LKR2,000 per person per entry whereas locals only pay a small fraction.

There is a cafe , ideally located by the large lawn if you want to stay longer/ are in need of refreshments.

review_text: One of the oldest botanical gardens in the world.  Our guide around the gardens was the botanist Bandara Palipana and he made it a most interesting tour.  We saw many trees and shrubs which were new to us and the stories behind some of the plantings was interesting.  The orchis collection has over 300 varieties on show.  The Cook pine (introduced from New Caledonia by Captain Cook) is unusual as always leans towards the equator.   HM Queen Elizabeth II, Lord Mountbatten, King George IV, Yuri Gagarin and others have planted trees there.  Lord Mountbatten used the old residence in the centre f the park as his headquarters as Supreme Allied Commander of South East Asia Command during WWII.  The gardens are kept in a pristine condition.  Many Bollywood films have used it for location shooting.
