review_text:
Yes there are a lot of jeeps, but I felt this park was more open and avoided a lot of the crush I felt with Yala National Park (the highlight being to try and spot an elusive Sri Lankan leopard or Sloth Bear).  The jeeps on this occasion had room to manoeuvre and the elephants were all very obliging and all jeeps kept their distance and even waited if elephants approached to let them have their way.  So I did enjoy this park much more - seeing elephant families doing their own thing without being hassled by the jeeps was most enjoyable.  Birdlife was the only other wildlife but there were large and small herds everywhere in this park and I didn't feel the jostling of jeeps too much.  Most drove up slowly, found a position and parked to allow us to take photographs or just enjoy their antics.  On our safari I didn't feel that the jeep drivers were encroaching on the elephants as all the jeeps seem to follow the track, parked off to the side and allowed us to just watch the elephants - yes mothers put their babies on the other side of the jeeps, but continued feeding, and the babies of course continued playing.

I actually quite enjoyed the afternoon safari as instead of getting hotter, it cooled as the afternoon sun began to set.  

We were a private group with our own guide so we had a pre-arranged driver for this attraction, so it was just us in a slightly newer and more comfortable jeep - open topped and a little dusty, but allowed you to stand and take photos when the jeep stopped.

Have an open mind here - Sri Lankan is a developing country and has a long way to go so don't expect the same level of eco-tourism you would get in other countries.

review_text: This is a good place to see elephants in the wild. Depending on your luck you may see 20 or more elephants in groups. It is a busy place. Lots of jeeps. Just make sure to be careful of low hanging branches and narrow passages through thick vegetation, especially on the way back once the safari is over. We saw one of the visitors got a cut on face after getting hit by a tree branch on the way back from safari. And it is an open top safari. So apply plenty of sun screen and wear good sun protection. Also it can be dusty and so bring a mask if you have dust allergies.

review_text: This is the perfect drive in the evening, even though we didn't have any plan of visiting this park, our guide suggested to do this, so we went ahead and we were not disappointed. It's an 2-3 hour long Safari in the park and they take you near the lake where elephants come there to eat. It's the perfect time to visit as you would end up seeing so many so close. I think they are used to so many jeeps coming close everyday so they were busy eating and we were ignored most of the time by them. So we closely watched how they eat the grass, the way they pull out, dust it out and then eat. It was an amazing experience to watch them so close. We were taken another side of the lake for a nice view which you can climb few stairs to watch and if you are keen just to get the legs dirty after. The surprising visitors were variety of birds, they were awesome. I wish I had more time to spot them more.

review_text: If you are looking for an exclusive observation of elephants grazing in herds by the lake edge you are going to be disappointed. This is a popular tourist attraction and the convoy of vehicles winding their way along the dirt roads to find elephants is at times intrusive. Having said that you are likely to have the opportunity to see groups of elephants as we did. There were many with young, one or two month old babies and they genuinely seemed unconcerned with the vehicles nearby. For the most part drivers showed some respect for the elephantÂ’s welfare and maintained a good distance. In many instances the elephants ambled slowly closer to the vehicles. If you decide to go my suggestion would be to go late afternoon, say from 3.00pm onwards. This way you escape the heat of the day. There are dozens of drivers outside the park entrance ready to take you.

review_text: This was our first (of 3) safari experiences in Sri Lanka.  The jeep was in average condition,  3 rows of seats,  with open roofs where you could stand up.  All the jeeps follow the same track,  up to 2 abreast at a time. You go through bush, then through a river (3 jeeps got stuck - fortunately not ours) and then it opens out to large areas surrounding the lake.   We saw a couple of hundred elephants (best to go on an afternoon safari as they come to the lake for water). Unfortunately there were almost as many jeeps as elephants and at first we sat in a huge queue (the jeeps at the front of the line didn't move on in a timely manner).  After a while the jeeps spread out and there were plenty more elephants to see,  with less crowded jeep conditions. Our driver didn't really talk to us,  but it was pretty obvious what we were looking at! If you're into elephants this is the safari for you.

review_text:
Sadly this wildlife park is being over-exploited, with convoys of jeeps in search of a limited number of elephants. When a herd was spotted, the dirt track turned into a 4x4 sales forecourt, with jeeps jostling for space and the best view.

We also saw a few larger birds (egrets, eagles, herons and pelicans), and a mongoose. 

Ironically, we saw two elephants (one of them with tasks, quite rare) by the side of the road on our drive back to the hotel. Our driver was quick to spot them in the semi-darkness, and we were much closer to them than in the wildlife park.

Our expectations may have been too high, as we had already visited Yala National Park earlier in our holiday. I would give Minneriya a miss and spend the extra time at Yala. A more diverse range of animals and birds, with less jeeps!!

Apart from the elephants you can see some other species like deer, wild boar, buffalo, etc. Be alert and get some information from your guide or any other local in the area about the crowd in the park as lots of crowd will ruin your experience.

review_text:
We were lucky to see many elephants and not get stuck in the mud in the park because our touring driver knew an excellent company who use 4 wheel drive jeeps. The company is part of the Mihini hotel on the main Polonnaruwa road at Habarana. 
Our jeep driver was Nimal and he was excellent at navigating the rough and very muddy terrain . We saw two other much swankier jeeps stuck in the mud waiting for rescue because they are not 4WD. Don't be fooled into getting one of those. Nimal is a local guy and knows a lot about elephants. He also managed to get us away from the other jeeps so a lot of the time when we saw elephants we were on our own which was a much better experience than being in a traffic jam of 8 of them. Highly recommended and seeing elephants in the wild and beautiful setting was very special.

review_text:
The "Ecco Park" is supposedly a sanctuary for wild elephants but it has now become completely over-commercialized by greedy Tours firms all congesting parts of the park in their diesel polluting vehicles.

We were on an organised trip that lasted several hours much of which was spent in traffic jams of vehicles all travelling along the same track but often several lines abreast and in different directions as individual drivers each sought to outdo the numerous other vehicles. Some broke down or attempted ridiculous "three-point turns" in the track only to become stuck in the mud thus causing various blockages. At one point we didn't move for nearly an hour. Imagine a crowded street full of tuck tuks all vying to get to the same spot and not caring about the chaos created and the effect on the elephants. 

Most importantly the Elephants' space isn't respected so they were sometimes chased by selfish drivers. It was an appalling experience for the animals and the far too numerous visitors alll congested into very tight areas. 

Website photos suggest large open spaces and numerous elephants enjoying the peaceful sanctuary but instead we saw a mere handful and on each occasion they were quickly approached from various directions by numerous jeeps. It's just become a commercial rip off for greedy firms. 

Overall it was chaotic, disrespectful of the elephants and an appalling excursion. Avoid!!!!

review_text: Sri Lankan safaris are perhaps the cheapest on the planet compared to Africa, but do understand, you will be in a queue of vehicles, the drivers will all be communicating with each other to get their convoys close to any animals spotted. On our safari the Elephants were clearly upset with being intruded upon. One of the vehicles got bogged and the Elephants were being quite aggressive. The interpretation from our guide was little more than "look - there's and elephant" He certainly was no naturalist. The national park was certainly beautiful, and it was nice to be out in the bush, but I would not describe this as an "eco" experience. Sri Lanka has a way to go to offer true eco tourism experiences.

It is the largest concentration and gathering of Asian elephants that can be seen anywhere in the world. We did an open top Jeep safari, watching baby elephants playing with each other, bull elephants tussling for dominance and the great matriarchs surveying the scene is not a sight you are likely to forget in a hurry. Inside the park you will also come across some wild boar, peacocks, deer and many more animals roaming freely as nature intended them to live. 
Aside from the elephant, Minneriya is also home to some 23 other species of mammals a paradise for many species of Lizard and you will see them here in all their colour if you look carefully enough. the views are stunning. You'll see hundreds of birds, storks, pheasants, beer eaters, herons, pelicans, eagles, etc. There are also spotted deerÂ’s roaming around. The driver was knowledgeable and would point at different species.  as well as snakes like the Indian Python and the Mugger Crocodile. Above all, of course, are Sri LankaÂ’s wonderfully varied bird population.
 We drove for over an hour seeing birds, butterflies, tortoises, deerÂ’s and when we thought viewings were over, we saw a young grey leopard. It was just breath-taking. Then more Stunning scenery and you will also encounter deer, buffalo, pelicans and peacocks. Despite the heat it was a great afternoon at the park. The drivers are constantly in contact with each other and updating where the elephants are to be seen. I highly recommend this to everyone.

The downside was the hordes of other safari vans and people in them. There was lots of congestion at the points were the elephants were and it did impede the experience slightly.  Some of the behaviour of other vans and the people in them left a lot to be desired and at times got to close and upset elephants.

Nevertheless it was a lovely site and one I wanted to see and would say donÂ’t miss the experience!

review_text: Went on a jeep safari as part of our Sri Lanka tour. Wonderful to see so many Asian elephants but it felt like the drivers were chasing down the elephants! There was nearly as many jeeps as elephants and it didnÂ’t seem much consideration was given to the wildlife, elephants especially. We have been on safari in Africa where there is a 2 vehicle limit to protect the animals from over exposure, this was certainly not the case here. Concerned how much of the money raised from the safari actually goes to the protection and conservation of these endangered animals, I believe it probably goes to purchasing more jeeps!! Would not give them my money again until I was convinced a large percentage was being used for conservation purposes. Their tactics and approach should be monitored by animal welfare groups to ensure it is in the animals interests.

Once at the entrance you have to pay for each individual in the jeep and there is a discount for jeeps with more people in so a couple will pay slightly more than a jeep with four and so on.

Once in the park it takes a while to reach the lake but we saw multiple elephants on the way, then two herds of about 30 elephants at the lake ranging in age and size from cute little ones to one of the largest who was only one of two with tusks.

What an incredible day, and our guide held right back and kept a good distance, where we saw others too close.

review_text:
We were almost bitterly disappointed as the park was closed on the day we wished to visit due to an employee strike, however it was resolved on our last day - worth checking that there are no such issues when you are planning to go.

The elephants gather early morning and during the evening, so going in the middle of the day will end in disappointment as the elephants head into the jungle. Worth booking in advance to make sure you get a good time slot.

The gathering is a daily ritual, so seeing elephants is highly likely.

The round trip is approx 2 hours, including about 30 minutes to get into the jungle lake where the elephants gather, so you can spend around an hour watching the various herds/families gather.

It was a great experience, and a "must do".

The elephants are not confined to the park. When returning to our hotel after dark, we saw an elephant on the road side, eating, so keep your eyes open!!!

We were lucky enough to get our own jeep, and they are comfortable. Drivers are knowledgeable and enthusiastic.

It's an unique experience.

review_text:
Minneriya is reputed to be the home of the largest herd of Asian Elephants, and our experience in April 2017 would seem to bear that out. Despite the commercialisation of the trip - there must have been 50+ Land Cruisers around the reservoir - the park is big enough to give one a good view of the herd, especially as it gathers in late afternoon before going into the forest to sleep. They came from all around, to drink, wash and play in the shallow waters, before setting off in a column and heading back into the forest - and they were so quiet. No squealing from the baby elephants, nor thudding of feet from the adults, but simply an inexorable susuration as they walked past us.

The area is also home to many other species, and we saw many types of bird, including the omni-present egrets, ibis and other water fowl. There are also crocodiles, and we saw a couple basking on the banks. A great experience.

My sister and I went to this park in mid Oct. Before setting off, we were told by the tour guide aka jeep driver that we might see peacock, buffalo, many species of bird, etc in the journey. Eventually we could only see big group of wild elephants. It was impressive to witness a crowd of 80+ giants in wild which totally opened my eye.

This was my first safari experience so I found it eye-opening. However it was the second safari visit of my sister and it disappointed her a bit comparing with her last visit in Udawalawa national park in the South of Sri Lanka. She saw a lot of peacock on tree, buffaloes, many birds in beautiful colors on top of elephants and to her the Udawalawa visit was more a memorable experience than Minneriya. 

For those who are planning a visit around the country, would recommend to visit other sizable national park where may have higher chance to see more wild animal instead of just elephants. If your trip cover just the middle part, this safari is still a must-go!

review_text: We were lucky enough to visit Minneriya National Park during The Gathering. This is a natural event that happens between June and October when elephants migrate to Minneriya for the protected area and large lake. It still depends on the day you visit but we saw over 200 elephants and a magnificent tusker who gave us a show bathing in the lake. Many new babies that were so enchanting to watch. Don't expect to be the only person in a safari jeep in the park... there will likely be many. We spent over 3 hours there with our driver and saw so much. We also encountered a water buffalo stampede with hundreds of them running right across our path! It was an unforgettable experience and one that I will treasure for years to come.

review_text:
It will be interesting to see what happens in future as they are building a tarmac road just about up to the national park.
It was great to see the elephants up close but they really need to educate the drivers more they formed a whole line blocking the groups of elephants actually getting over to the water hole at one point and one elephant was getting agitated and moving towards the jeeps to protect the small baby elephants which is completely understandable.
Our guide told us in the peak period there are over a 1,000 jeeps in the park- more jeeps than elephants.They really need to get the balance right-
It was interesting to see some groups of elephants waiting in the trees for the jeeps to go at sunset before starting to come out down to the water hole.
Good experience but they need to get the balance right otherwise the elephants will withdraw.
Interesting to also see cattle grazing and eating grass in the national park- the elephants food too....

review_text:
A must do on our agenda!

Piled into the back of jeeps (5 seats) & headed into the national park on a fine day with the roof open & no side wall giving great views. The driver was great driving along & spotting various animals in the bush and grass.

The highlight took a little time with us seeing various monkeys, birds & water buffalo before finding the elephants (a couple of large herds). The elephants were amazing - probably 50 to 80 in total & they were so carefree despite our close attendance.  At the busiest time there must have been 50 jeeps & 4wd's parked up with cameras clicking amongst many excited people. The elephants mainly ate grass however a few entered the lake.

We also ascended a small tower for better views over the countryside & lake - be careful as no handrails. Nothing special but part of the tour.

Took a bit of a drive back to the bus/car park where we met numerous monkeys & a couple of relatively tame deer.  Great fun even for the older less mobile folk in our group.

review_text:
Don't go to other "sanctuaries", visit Minneriya if you want to see elephants in their natural environment, thriving, playing and reproducing in a healthy setting. We did a 3 hour "safari". There's not a huge amount to see apart from elephants, but there are lots of then and you can get close to them (closest was about 10 metres from the jeep). The safari is basic but fun, you park in the car park, climb in the back of a jeep and get driven around the park to seek out the elephants. We went in the afternoon as that's when they are most likely to congregate at the lake. Our jeep driver was very good, the two of us bounced around in the back - just two side benches, three padded cross bars to hold onto if you want to stand up. No Health & Safety here - hold on tight to avoid bashing your bits against the side of the jeep, and if standing, duck to avoid branches thwacking you in the face! Remember sun cream as there's no cover, and a hat is risky to blow off if there's wind. 

We saw loads of elephants - noisy, playful, muddy, but and small. There was one suckling it's mother, still a bit pink, that our driver said was about ten days old. 

We did this as part of a four day tour which originally had the elephant sanctuary in its itinerary, but switched to Minneriya before we travelled. We are so pleased, as people concerned with animal welfare, opposed to elephant tricks and rides and tethering, but still wanting to be close to the magnificent beasts.

review_text:
It was great to see such large numbers of elephants in the family groups - matriarch, babies, youngsters, teenagers. Then with the young males who had been kicked out from the herd just feeding a short way from the main herd.  Interesting to watch the antics of some larger males finding their way into the smaller herds to check out the females.   

Yes there are a lot of safari jeeps but it did not seem as chaotic as in the Yala National Park and I think this is due to the fact that this park has a rather large open area of grass around lakes that allow for the army of jeeps to park by the road and allow for viewing by everyone as there were elephants everywhere.  In Yala once an elusive leopard is found, it's a race on for ever driver to get their clients a sighting and the tracks are narrow and not as open as in Minneriya.

I loved watching the babies, and yes the protective mothers keeping their bodies to the jeep side, but both continued grazing whilst we looked on. Watching elephant behaviour was interesting -  a mother comin out from a bamboo thicket as we approached in the jeep.  We stopped. She stopped. She waited - we didn't move.  Then obviously when she thought it was safe, she signalled to the two younger elephants and one by one out of the thicket they came and crossed the track.

I didn't feel the driver of our safari jeep hassled the elephants at all.  All the jeeps seemed to give them the space. If the elephant came behind the jeep, the driver stopped, waited for the elephant to pass or do what it wanted, before the driver proceeded along the track   The park appears to have designated trails that the vehicles can use and the jeeps generally stated on this track or to the side if they needed to pass.

Its main purpose for this park I think is for wild elephant viewing, but we also saw lots of birdlife around the lake.

We did an afternoon safari from 3pm and I found the seats were very nicely padded in our vehicle but seatbelts I think are optional, but then I was standing up a lot when the vehicle was parked or moving slowly along.

It's not for everyone as it's hot, it's bumpy, but I enjoyed it.

review_text:
We saw lots of elephants, and the park is a nice setting. I agree with some other reviews that, if it's busy, there are a number of jeeps, and you can smell the pollution from them, which made me feel bad about doing the safari. 

I used fasttur to book in advance. I am not sure whether they are overcharging or whether they charge the standard rate for entrance+jeep hire. But there is no visible benefit from their service, as you still have to wait for the driver to purchase the tickets. If there is a queue, that can be a while. But still, it guarantees you a jeep. They did say an English-language guide would be included, but that was not the case at all. In the end, you don't need one anyway, but I feel they should have given a discount for something they did not provide.

Thoroughly enjoyed our visit. We must have seen between 80 -90 elephants, often in groups of 8 to 10, all females with young. The males are only around in June/July at mating time. 

We did get really close up to them and they did not seem in the least bit bothered by the jeeps and the elephants were not chased at all by the jeeps. The jeep ride is like a bucking bronco. We did not see nearly as many elephants in Yala. 

Don't bother with distant photos with half hidden elephants as you will see plenty up close.

review_text: This is one of three 'safaris' we did in Sri Lanka, and was by far the least enjoyable. It seems that there is little regard for the environment or the wildlife as a large number of vehicles thrash around a relatively small area. I had the feeling that the tour was not about the wildlife at all, but about giving tourists a four wheel drive experience - not what we signed up for. The park itself appears to be in a sad state with many invasive weed species; the roads are overused by the heavy vehicle traffic and poorly maintained. We saw a few elephants, but the experience was marred by the volume of jeeps jostling for position. review_text:
Although we hired a private Jeep it wasn't quite the intimate experience you imagine. Transfer to the park from the hotel was swift, I'm fairly certain our driver was trained by Lewis Hamilton. Entry to the park is chaotic with the car park heaving with other vehicles waiting to get in followed by a long wait to start moving along a dusty track bumper to bumper. I never imagined eyes watering with dust & exhaust fumes that you would see anything but our expert tracker seemed to know that if there were 30 or so jeeps huddled together there might be something worth seeing.
Once you see the elephants and there are plenty including some only weeks old, all you can do is focus on  them. They switch off the engines and you can watch at close range as they go about eating with their young rolling in the mud.We even saw some tuskers that the guide said are quite rare.
It was a good afternoon & although they probably allow too many vehicles in I wanted to go as much as the next person & enjoyed being so close to the elephants.

review_text:
We were staying at Habarana and its a 15 min drive to the entrance of the National park. The ticket price calculation is a bit weird as all price lists are displayed in the local language only . Three of us in a JEEP cost me SL Rupees 9840 as entrance fees for us and jeep driver  plus SLR 5000 for the jeep rental . Wish the prices were better explained in English as is done at other places. We were lucky to have the services of Kavinda Thushan (kavindathushan888@gmail.com) who ensured that we moved in at the appropriate time ie 3pm and saw atleast 3 large groups of wild elephants , including a solo rogue tusker. All in all we would have seen 70-80 elephants. It is a bit tricky as there is another national park , across the road (name starting with K) . Elephants keep on moving and there are times when sighting wud be nil in Minneriya as all elephant herds would have moved across the road to the other park. 
We spent time till 5:30 pm in the park and saw elephants of all sizes from very small babies to large tuskers. Water buffaloes also inhabit this park and so do peacocks , monkeys and other animals. There is a huge lake inside the park called Habarana lake which attracts all wild animals.
Definitely worth a visit. Take your camera and binocs as they would be handy.

review_text: If you intend to see a lot of elephants enjoying in their natural habitat, eating, drinking and having fun, this is the place for you. Our driver had a contact for the jeep safari and thus we didnÂ’t book in advance. The park is vast, full of greenery and spread across nearly 9000 hectares. As it was a weekday, there were not much people, just a few jeeps doing the safari. The site of more than 60-70 elephants at one place, enjoying their time, was really beautiful and satisfying. Plenty of playful baby elephants seen!! There are a lot of bird species as well in the park. Our safari driver was sharp-eyed and knowledgeable, spotting and identifying birds at a distance and stopping to let us take photos. The safari took nearly 2.5 hours to complete. All in all, it was worth the price paid for!!

review_text: There are monkeys, various species of birds and water buffalo a plenty to get you excited but we were very fortunate to see two different elephant herds at close range. The first was a reasonably large herd which were by the waters edge. This herd had many adult elephants and three young tuskers. The second herd crossed the road directly, and very close to, the rear of our stationary jeep. They were almost in touching distance, amazing animals to get so close to. Again we were lucky enough to see yet another mid aged tusker. It is advisable to cover yourself up well and to use plenty of sun cream as the jeep is open top and the sun is unrelenting. A must do activity for anyone lucky enough to get the opportunity to do so.

review_text:
WeÂ’ve been on one safari in india to see tigers and have left dismayed and poorer because it of course is down to luck and on on both occasions saw nothing more than a bird or monkey. So the thought of doing a safari to possibly see elephants was not top of our list in Sri Lanka. 

But our driver said we wouldnÂ’t be disappointed so we gave it a go. 

First impressions great - we had our own jerk and driver. None of the group squeezing into one huge jeep for twenty with limited views. 

As we entered the National Park and drove around for 15mins I started to recognise in myself that desperation you feel looking for anything, something to make you think you just MIGHT see an animal. After another five minutes we slowed down and poking its head through some palms was a huge elephant munching on some food. 

That alone left us happy and content as it had already surpassed expectations. Amazing 

We then drove around the corner and found ourselves surrounded - literally surrounded by a herd of about 300 elephants. All slowly eating and gradually edging toward a lake for water. 

We saw families, babies and even rare tusked elephants (apparently only about 6% have tusks here). Words cannot describe the experience. We slowly drive around with them for an hour finding it hard to pull ourselves away. We eventually did to drive around another corner of the lake only to have another herd of about 200 doing the same. 

There is nothing more amazing than watching the sunset and these amazing animals calmly go about their business with no fear of humans or the Jeep and most importantly in their natural habitat living wild. 

Make sure you do this. It was an experience of a lifetime and the highlight of two weeks in Sri Lanka

review_text: Our driver Chathu from Sri Lanka Wide Tours arranged this at short notice with his friend Amila, a jeep driver at the park. The 2 of them really made this a great experience but you really have to get over the sheer volume of other jeeps at the waters edge where all the elephants congregate to get the most out of this. There were alot of elephants to see including a family with a week old baby. You could watch them all for hours and its a great setting with the lake as a backdrop. Amila managed to get us off the beaten track and away from the masses for most of the trip where we were able to see a variety of birds, monkeys, lizards and deer. There were no bears or leopards to be seen but elephants are what you come to see here for the most part. We came across a wounded elephant alone in the bush on the way back. Apparently the park was aware of it but inter-departmental politics and red tape was preventing something being done about it. The elephant was clearly in pain. Chathu and Amila both called the ministers office in Colombo while we were there and ended up getting something done about it. The calls were flying back and forward to Amila. We were very impressed by his tenacity in trying to get something done about it.

review_text:
This park is just off the main road from Habarana to Polynaruwa. We took a jeep "safari" ............. which means you stand up in the back of a jeep, holding on to the roll bars.
Nothing much to see as you enter down a dusty track - but then it opens out to a flat area by the lake, where there are a lot of elephants ..................and a LOT of jeeps!
Some of the jeep drivers could do with better training, as they get too close and spook the animals - but its still goo and there are plenty of birds to see by the lake.
Not really a safari, but quite an interesting drive around for around 2-3 hours.
The good news is that they only allow the jeeps in between 6am and 6pm - no night time drives .................but there are a LOT of jeeps. They need to be careful or they'll spoil this by unregulated commercialism.

review_text:
Minneriya National Park is on the way to Polonruwa, just around 10 Kms from Habarana town. You have lot of options from jeep drivers and hotels, guest house who can organize the safari into the national park. 

Its best to visit the park in the afternoon at 3 pm as you have better chance of sighting elephants & other animals, birds in the park. The Jeep safari should not cost more than LKR (Srilankan Rupees) 3500-4000 for the entire jeep. The entrance tickets to the park is steep but worth the price.

The jeep can seat easily 6 persons. Check out the jeep before you agree on confirming the same. Go for Jeep which is more open type with good space to stand and view the wildlife. Some jeeps have 2-3 rows of seats which makes the jeep cramped and no space to stand for viewing animals.

The Park has dense population of elephants. You are sure to sight elephants at close proximity specially near the lake within the park. Apart from Elephants there are quite a few birds you can sight near the lake and water bodies within the park. 

The safari is for 2 hours and almost all the Jeep Drivers are knowledgeable about the route within the park and places to sight elephants. The Jeep safari has a pit stop at lake where you can get down and take pictures. There is tower near the pit stop to get views of lake and park.

Overall a must visit place if you are staying in Habarana or near by place.

review_text:
While visiting Sirigiya, we decided to visit Minneriya National Park and it was the best decision we could make.
I have seen but reviews of people saying it was crowded. It must have been we went late during the day, but we just came across 2 more jeeps in the whole safari
We arrived just after 3pm. We were travelling with locals who arranged a safari driver that was at the entrance for only Rs3000 (bear in mind that you may be overcharged if you don't have someone to negotiate it). The entrance fee is almost none for locals and quite higher for foreigners, but still quite reasonable. 
We started the safari and were able stand up on the jeep and get amazing views. The first part of the route is a dense forest, but when you reach the opening, the views are stunning. You'll see hundreds of birds, storks, pheasants, beer eaters, herons, pelicans, eagles, etc. There are also spotted deers roaming around. The driver was knowledgeable and would point at different species. We saw elephants far away, then, a lonely one 50 meters away and then we came close to three, i.e. a mum with the two kids. We were totally amazed at seeing wild animals at less than 30 meters away and suddenly the protective and caring mother charged at us. It was terrifying yet astounding. The mum just wanted to ensure that we didn't hurt her kids. 
We drove for over an hour seeing birds, butterflies, tortoises, deers and when we thought viewings were over we saw a young grey leopard. It was just breathtaking, but the young fellow disappeared before we got our cameras out so it only got imprinted in our memories.
Overall, we spent 2 hours enjoying beautiful views and spotting some of Sri Lankan amazing wild life. Highly recommended.

Here you have the chance to get up really close and personal to the wild elephants. We saw a family of 5 and it was amazing, as well as seeing other elephants along the way. We were under the impression beforehand that we would see hundreds of elephants but unfortunately this was not the case, so don't get your hopes up. This did not ruin the experience as it is really amazing to see wild elephants so closely in their natural habitat. We saw about 11 in total.

There are also other animals here to see such as lizards, iguanas, monkeys, water buffalos etc. 

We spent over 3 hours in the safari but the time flew by. A must do if you are in the area.

review_text:
I am not an elephant person.  Never have been.  I would see an elephant or two at the zoo and be ..... meh.  But Minneriya ... ROCKED. MY. WORLD.

It starts with a 30 minute ride in a jeep from the entrance into the heart of the national park.  The roads are good, you can stand up in the back of the jeep and you are racing through the jungle with the wind in your hair; exhilarating!  And we hadn't seen our first elephant yet!

During the next three hours, we encountered lone male elephants (who challenged our small jeep for dominance), a young mum with babies in tow (who was determined to chase us away to protect her babies) and then a herd by the lake.  The herd must have been close to 200 elephants; the sight was mesmerising.  Groups of elephants bathing, males warily standing apart watching the jeeps and each other, baby elephants running excitedly from group to group tooting their little trunks.  It was the most gorgeous experience.

And it is not just elephants, we also saw flocks of birds, a herd of water buffalo and one crocodile sub-bathing.

A brilliant afternoon, we loved this experience so much that we almost considered going back a second time!

I have been so looking forward to this and it exceeded my expectations! We were picked up from our accommodation and had a 20 minute drive to the park entrance. The roads inside are bumpy and dusty but we were by ourselves for quite a while and it did take a while to find a family group. We stopped and just watched in awe as they ate and move a bit and are some more. We moved on and saw some deer, monkeys and a turtle sunning itself then turned around and the group of elephants had trebled in number. A lot of other jeeps did join us and it got rather crowded but everyone switched their engines off and just enjoyed the view!
I felt really privileged to have had this experience and definitely recommend!

Talk about a major disappointment, for our 3 kids and us! When we got out of the park, there were many, many jeeps that were coming in .  Hopefully for them, and they saw more elephants than we did during the day. 

The entrance fee was 11,000 roupies for the 5 of us (2 adults + 3 children) + 5,000 roupies for the jeep/driver, so this was a very expensive outing.

review_text:
Wow, wow and wow!

I have been on safari in South Africa before but never have I seen herds of elephants congregating NATURALLY in their hundreds. So close you could almost touch them but there of their own accord and not through force or any sort of zoo/conservation set up. 

Nature at its absolute best. I highly recommend this nature reserve to all! 

You could sit there all day just staring and would never get bored. Such majestic animals without humans on their backs or chains around their feet. Playing in the water, eating grass and just being elephants!

review_text:
Apart from having to get up at 3am for the drive there the day was well worth the effort.
The guides were all very friendly but driving around the bumpy roads of the reserve in the back of a pickup truck safari car was uncomfortable.
We saw all the animals from families of Elephants to Monkeys crocodiles water buffalo wild bore and many more.
The visit to the Elephant orphanage at feeding time was my highlight.
About 6 babies at a time let in running grabbing the pipes of the feeding tubes in their mouths to get their funnels of milk was magnificent to witness.
Highly recommended.

review_text:
We enjoyed an amazing safari experience with a private guide called Lahiru. He organised everything for us- our transfer from Ella to the National Park, where we had our fantastic 4-hour safari, and our transfer on to Mirissa. During the safari Lahiru was very knowledgeable and enthusiastic- it was great to have a guide who clearly loved and respected the animals, while making sure we had an incredible safari experience- it was clear he wanted to give us the best experience possible! There are quite a lot of jeeps in the park but Lahiru managed to bring us places to see animals in secluded areas with no one else around where we got closer than we could ever have imagined to lot of animals including elephants- our highlight!! We got some amazing photos and memories to last a lifetime.

We would recommend booking Lahiru if you are looking for a guide for the safari. (We contacted him directly on +94 76 272 6799)

review_text:
We had a perfect day in Udawalawe National Park, thanks to Lahiru who organized everything from A to Z: he sent a driver who picked us up at our hotel near Tangalle, drove us to Ella afterwards and then back to our hotel.
The safari was the most incredible experience in Sri Lanka so far! We saw a teenage male elephant bathing himself and were only a few metres away, four female elephants and one adult male elephant... Besides the elephants, we saw crocodiles, hyenas, different kinds of birds and chameleons, mungos, deers, wild boars and probably more. Almost everytime we were completely alone, not one other jeep was there besides us. When we arrived at the lake, we were the only ones seeing about ten crocodiles, elephants, birds and hyenas at once. Lahiru knows all the roads and places and seems to suspect which animals will be where and when. This made this trip so special. He is also a very funny guy and cares a lot about the park and the animals. Thank you a lot for this unforgettable trip. See you in Cologne... Katja + Halil
You can reach Lahiru via Whatsapp or phone: +94 762726799

review_text:
A beautiful park with a big (men made) lake. Around the lake are many kind of animals. Mainly birds and elephants. 
We had a afternoon drive and have seen lots of elephants, birds, crocodiles and many more. 
I would recommend going here and there are several places to stay close to the entrance of the park. You can arrange your safari right at the entrance by hiring a driver, car and guide and pay for the entrance fee separately. Or you can arrange a package via your hotel. 

The downside of the park is the plastic rubbish people leave in the park. I really canÂ’t believe this is happening and not be cleaned by the authorities in a national park. I hope the local people will understand some day the importance of a clean environment for nature.

Initially felt a bit like a traffic jam of jeeps but they go different ways and it then got much better.
Had a wonderful moment with a group of female elephants with three babies arriving at a water hole to wash and throw dust on themselves. 
Lots of buffalo, birds, and several crocs. Spent over three hours driving around the bumpy tracks which was enough for the 2 year old.
Worth a visit!

review_text:
We had a great morning on safari at Udawalale National Park. We got picked up from our homestay (FalconÂ’s Nest) at 5am and waited in the queue. Lots of drivers like to go nice and early to get in quickly - the animals are better in the morning & you usually see more.

The sun rising as we travelled through the park was amazing. 

We saw so many elephants - one came so close that our guide had to reverse! We also saw crocodiles, water buffalo, wildcats, jeckalls, peacocks (hundreds of them!) and lots of other birds. Unfortunately no leopards for us but as there are only approx 15 in the whole park, itÂ’s very unusual to see them!

We barely saw any other jeeps throughout our 3.5 hours in the park and were able to watch the elephants so peacefully with only one other jeep. 

Highly recommend Udawalale if youÂ’re wanting to see elephants :) Booking through your hotel/homestay is the best option as they tend to have a guide they use. You can also visit the Elephant Transit Home after and see the elephants being fed!

After reading reviews on TA we decided to take a safari. We simply WhatsApp Lahiru, who has been mentioned many times & he made all the arrangements. 
A driver picked us up from our Villa, we switched into LahiruÂ’s jeep at the entrance, did a 4 hour ride around & then back home. It was quite a long day with lots of traveling. 
We found him very informative & had a keen eye to spot thing we could never have seen. 
We seemed lucky in that we saw so many elephants all over the park, including 1 week old calves who could barely walk in a straight line without falling over. 
Also plenty of birds, buffalo, lizards, a few crocodile, red spotted deer, monkeys & giant squirrels. 
The tracks around were rutted in places but thatÂ’s to be expected. The jeeps everybody seems to use are clearly up to job & make for a great experience.

review_text:
We were staying at a fairly newly opened local hotel: Royal Reach Family Resort (1/2hr drive from the National Park) and their lovely staff helped us organise this unforgettable 3 hour long safari in their hotel jeep. They also promised to get us an English speaking guide who turned out to be an absolute expert on all the wonderful creatures (and plants!) to be seen there. We picked him up at the entrance of the National Park and with our guide on board our safari was off to a great start. 
Lakshan is a volunteer guide and he turned out to be a real expert. He worked closely with the driver to take us away from the crowds into the heart of the park, spotting herd after herd of elephants, filling us with exciting facts and anecdotes about each animal encountered along the way: peacocks perched on top of tall trees, gorgeous birds of all shapes and colours, lizards and buffaloes. Lakshan has a very extensive knowledge of the fauna and flora of Udawalawe Park and he is a skilled educator, too, He taught us how to recognise different species, how to tell the age and sex of the elephants, His enthusiasm for this place was contagious. Lakshan is also very patient so throughout the trip we had plenty of time to take fantastic pictures without being rushed. The three hours we spent with him exploring the national park were the highlight of our Sri Lankan trip. The whole safari for two people was about $60 including the jeep, entrance fees and a voluntary contribution to our guide! I cannot recommend him highly enough. 
If you would like to contact Lakshan - you can find him on Facebook: Lakshan Geeganaarachchi (he was the guide for Prince Edward- Earl of Essex and his wife when they visited Udawalawe last year!). He is brilliant!

review_text: This is not like a safari in Africa as predators are few. Many of the park's secrets were revealed over a 3H safari. The birding is very good, bee eaters posing for you. The elephants steal the show. We had herds eating grass and crossing the road. At the end of the day there were three elephants, one a baby, drinking at a waterhole; epic stuff. The water areas produced their own attractions, from crocodiles with open mouths to cormorants drying their open wings to lounging water buffaloes. The roads are in fair condition with just a bit of dust to be expected. The park is largely forested with areas of bush. Any number of companies will take you for hopefully what will be as good a day there as I had.

review_text:
Our first safari experience and we really enjoyed it. 
I would say to make sure your guides are good as ours was awful, we got no information other than pointing to the animals and naming them- wow. (Don't know the name but booked through capital lanka/ BH lanka). But this didn't ruin the experience and seeing the elephants in the wild was wonderful. 
The first hour was quiet we maybe only saw 2-3 elephants, peacock and a land monitor. But when we went to the clearing by the lake there was 10s of elephants, birds, spotted deer, water buffalo, a crocodile in the distance, painted stork, and a mongoose. 
Make sure you take water and suncream with you and maybe a snack too as a large part is of course waiting around to find the animals. (Most of the cars we saw are covered but depending on time of day the sun still comes through the sides).
The timing was right for us at about 3 hours, we knew a day tour or several days wouldn't interest us so great taster and amazing to see these animals in the wild.

review_text:
Entry fees skyrocketed about 2 weeks ago. Solo travelers pay $43USD, which is about $7USD more than two travelers entering together and so on ($43USD for individuals vs $36 USD if you're a couple). Also, as a point of reference the current entrance fee for Kruger National Park in South Africa is $27USD. $43USD is an extremely high entrance fee for any National Park in the world.  I know there's a cost savings on vehicles when you share one, but a solo traveler penalty is ridiculous. 

I tried to find people at the gate entrance to share a safari with. Many of the tourists were interested,  but the guides have a "mafia" type "wilderness association" and refused to let any tourists share costs.

Was it worth it? Maybe once. Well, when others described "herds of elephants" in their reviews, I was expecting herds, like in Tanzania, Kenya or like other places in Africa.  I believe herds in Sri Lanka means families of elephants, which numerically speaking are smaller-- maybe 5 or 6 in a family vs 10+ in Africa. There is a good variety of wildlife-- elephants, deer, monkeys, buffalo, crocodiles, mongoose, jackals, boar, peacocks and other birds. It was nice. 

If you're interested in going, I eventually went with the owner of my homstay, Nalaka, +94 77 635 8192. He took me on a 4 hour jeep safari for 8,500 rp. He was great at spotting birds baby elephants, and other wildlife that other guides who denied me didn't see.

review_text: I was quite surprised, the terrain was quite like many African safaris we have been on, clay roads, very uneven in parts but very picturesque. Places you would like to stop and just wait to see if any animals cross your path. In addition to elephants, and we saw many, there were spotted deer, sambar, crocodile, jackal, water buffalo, lots and lots of peacocks in display and many other birds. Elephants were single males sometimes but also several large family groups. And nice picturesque spots to just sit in quiet and wait to see if anything passes out of the bush. Our guide from Induwaru Safari Resort where we stayed was exceptional. Care was taken when driving not to disturb animals, plenty of time allowed for viewing to our requirements, effort obviously put in not to follow the crowd. Breakfast was taken on safari, sandwiches, egg, pancakes, fruit juice and fruit. A mobile breakfast better than many we have been served in the accommodations.

review_text:
We had an incredible time in Udawalawe Â– in large part because we booked with the incredible Mansala Safari Resort. Whether staying in their beautiful hotel or just taking their safari, we canÂ’t recommend them enough Â– theyÂ’re one of the best choices IÂ’ve made while travelling.

Mansala basically arrange everything Â– safari, binoculars, transit, entry to the national park Â– and you pay at the end. It was one of the cheapest options we found but also one of the best.

TironÂ’s guide Tharanga took us on our safari.  Like Tiron, heÂ’s locally born and a genuine animal lover. He did everything the guidebooks tell you youÂ’ll want in a guide Â– he was respectful of the animals, never crowded them, avoided hotspots full of other drivers, gave us information without overloading us, and showed us everything. 

We saw:
-	A herd of baby elephants
-	Crocodiles
-	Water buffalo
-	Lots of deer, including stags and, essentially, bambi
-	A family of wild boar, including 8 gorgeous little piglets running about in what my partner called Â‘the best thing IÂ’ve ever seenÂ’
-	Lots of birds, including peacocks, storks, different types of eagles, woodsand pipers, little green bee eaters (really beautiful), cormorants, lapwings, hoopoes
-	A surprise tortoise
-	Surprise mongeese

You can do an evening or morning safari, or both. We did an evening safari, which finishes before 6pm; we arrived at 2pm and went straight out onto it, which was more than enough time.

The hotel itself is a lovely family-run operation, with two rooms and the family living in the building. Despite the homey, personal feel, everything from the food to the rooms to the safari is of the highest possible standard.

Food is cooked by the family, eaten on the veranda with animals around Â– and is some of the best we ate on our trip. Eat there rather than going out into Udawalawe.

The room was one of the best we stayed in in Sri Lanka, despite often paying significantly more than at Mansala Â– beautiful, comfortable, well-equipped, modern Â– everything we needed. 

Tiron, who runs the place, is a really kind and generous man. He was born in the house youÂ’re staying in, knows the local area really well, and was one of our favourite people we met in Sri Lanka. When the driver heÂ’d booked for our 2-hour drive to Mirissa was suddenly unavailable, he took us himself. His number is +94 77 795 9090 - he's given us permission to share it, and is very responsive to WhatsApps.

If you want a really ethical, personal, kind experience, we canÂ’t recommend Tiron, Tharanga and Mansala enough. We had a really special time, with really special people.

review_text:
Before our first holidays in Sri Lanka we tried to get some information and tipps about a game drive in the Udawalawe National Park. One name appeared again and again with only very excited positive reviews: Lahiru (Whatsapp +94 76 272 6799). We contacted him about 2 weeks before our trip and booked a Safari (1/2 day). We were very curious - is there a difference to other guides? Well, the first difference was: he even helped us to organize a driver who picked us up in after our train-journey in Ella and brought us to Udawalawe, which was very herpful. Yesterday we had our Safari with Lahiru. He picked us up at the hotel at 2 p.m. and then  ... the whole afternoon was just AWESOME and OVERWHELMING!!!  Lahiru is a very good Jeep-driver who really knows the park and all it's hidden paths. Most of the time we didn't see any other safari-jeeps (while many others were driving in small convoys on the "main roads") ... but therefore more animals than we expected to see! Elephants - of course (once we were lucky to stop close to some elephants an after some minutes we found ourselfs in the middle of a herd - and buffalos, deers, some crocodiles, gold-jackals, mungos, 3 differend types of eagles, ... and lots of birds (pelicans, toucans, bee-eaters, peacocks, ...) and even the fresh trace of a leopard. It was ... NO WORDS! Lahiru knows a lot about all these animals, his eyes seem to see everything while he is driving  - it was perfect. He can also name some of the animals in German. I can recommend him as safari-guide without any doubt!

And don't forget to visit the elephant-orphanage. They take care about orphants from outside the national park and set them free in the park when they are grown up. You can watch the feeding - cued! Very affordable and definitely worth it!

review_text:
We booked our tour in the park about 2 weeks before our holiday in Udawalawe. Many travellers on tripadvisor recommended Lahiru as the most competent guide. And we totally agree. He is very aware of the smallest signs of  animals. Birds, lizzards, mungos and even footsteps of a leopard in the sand..he sees it all, while driving his huge car safely and carefully over the bumpy road. He led us to places, where no other car was seen and we had the honour to see about 35-40 elephants..even 2 babys. We didn't drive in a konvoi and it seemed, that every time a car came close, we took the other way. So we had the opportunity to take fabulous pics. It was such an amazing experience..I'm still speechless and will remember this for the rest of my life. 
The park itself is such a gorgeous place..peacefull and quiet. You can hear so many sounds of nature. We would have liked to take a rest at the lake for a couple of hours to just sit and enjoy the scenery. 
Next time Sri Lanka we definitly will come back and make a visit. You should too and definitly contact Lahiru, he is very reliable and even organized a driver for our next destination. His number you can contact with Whatsapp is: +94 762726799

review_text:
We took a 3 hr Safari booked through Viator with Bentota Travel. Bentota Travel is another story so i'm not going to say anything about that. 
We arrived at the reserve after going to the elephant sanctuary and transferred to a Jeep. Access to the jeep required climbing in through a narrow gap at the back of the vehicle while standing on a Beer crate!!! Not easy for a couple of portly nearly 60 year olds, but it makes for a good story afterwards!!
We engaged the services of a guide ( they do not charge as such, you just tip them at the end of the safari what you think their services were worth) I would thoroughly recommend getting a guide. We didn't know where to look and the driver is too busy keeping his eye on the track to spot for you. In the end it was so worth having him as he was able to point out Monitors, Lizards, and birds that we just wouldn't have spotted. 
We saw wild buffalo, jackals, numerous colourful birds and birds of prey, Turtles, Lizards, Monitors and Loads of Elephants. We were lucky enough to see a family group of about 10 elephants along with 2 week old calf, a couple of smaller family groups, numerous single elephants (Including one asleep leaning against a tree!), but the highlight was a Mother and Calf pair who crossed the track in front of us and went to the lake edge to drink. They then proceeded to bathe and play in the water. 
At the same time, they were surrounded by buffalo complete with storks standing on their backs (I kid you not!!)
All in all, an amazing 3 hrs and some of it quite emotional. We didn't seem to drive for more than a couple of minutes without seeing something. We did however meet some Landrovers with tourists and guide who had been in the park for 2 hrs and hadn't seen anything more than a couple of birds. i think we were extremely lucky and we happened to drop on a good guide who knew his stuff. Amazing Experience.

P.s. Getting out of the Jeep was much easier, I went out through the front Drivers window!!!!

review_text: I booked myself & partner in for an 8 hour tour of Udawalawe which we visited today, we choose Lahiru Prasad as our guide on a friends recommendation & TA reviews & booked him via Whatsapp (+94 76 272 6799). The National Park itself has amazing scenery, lagoons, bush & jungle along with lots of wildlife. We saw many different bird species including hawk, horn bills, fish owl, hummingbird, bee-eaters & jungle fowl, along with crocodiles, spotted deer, chameleons, mongoose, monitor lizards, wild boar and a pack of the rarely spotted golden jackal! We also saw 30 Elephants, solo males & herds of females along with 2 babies, one of which was only 2 months old. Most of our elephant spottings were just us alone with no other jeeps around, we were able to sit with a herd of females & baby eating grass around the jeep for over half an hour! Without sounding like an advert this was 100% down to Lahiru, he knows the park very well & took us on different trails to find the animals that other jeeps werenÂ’t on. HeÂ’s super knowledgeable about all the animals & answered any questions we had & managed to spot animals other jeeps with just a driver were driving past & missing. As it is also mating season the male elephants were quite difficult to approach, despite this we felt very safe & confident in LahiruÂ‘s Jeep. Over the 8 hours Lahiru was still stopping & showing us things until we left the park, being so close to the elephants was an unforgettable experience, thank you Lahiru & driver & Udawalawe National Park! Lahiru also took us for a proper local curry afterwards & organised a very well priced taxi on to Ella for us!

Everything about the safari was professional and enjoyable. I would absolutely recommend Lahiru for safari.

Due to our visit in Sri Lanka this safari was on our list so we couldn't wait to feel the amazing experience being in nature, in the heart of a jungle where wild life exists and live.
After having spend around 2 hours and a half driving from Hikkaduwa and made a short stop to Elephant transit home to see the orphan elephants we took the special jeep for the safari. The day was perfect for such an activity warm but not hot and partly cloudy. Our driver was very good and was able to found all the hidden animals around the area, also very well educated regarding the animals and their bahviour.
We had so great time as we met a lot elephants alone or families, bulls, snake, peacocks, many birds and some crocodile and all in very close distance, like being part of this place. We met the youngest Elephant of the safari which was 4 months old next to his mother and the oldest which was 45 years old.
A great experience that we strongly recommend to all tourists that is going to visit Sri Lanka. Also is not a so expensive tour.
We had this tour with Norlanka Tours which are very good and very well organised company.

review_text:
We enjoyed our afternoon jeep Safari with Lahiru on the 17th in some fabulous weather. The safari jeep had six seats which we had all for ourselves - a group of 2 adults and 2 children. Lahiru had some water and snacks for us and he took us on off-beaten paths with no other jeeps around. 

Out in the park we saw eagles, bee-eaters, jackals, turtles, a croc, storks, pelicans, spotted deer, a hornbill, a magnificent brown fish owl, monitor lizards, kingfishers, cormorants, the ubiquitous peacocks and at least five herds of elephants spread across different locations totalling around fifty in all, some with one-month old babies. That I guess was pretty much everything one could spot in the park. Lahiru made us spend about twenty minutes close to a herd with baby elephants. It was exhilarating to see these mighty beasts in their eye, so close up. LahiruÂ’s photography skills were excellent too! The drive back past the Udawalawe reservoir in fading light was also awesome. 

I would say, this was well worth the 150$ for 4-hours of absolute bliss - we must have covered at least 40kms in all. We had chosen Lahiru based on the glowing TA reviews and boy, he did not disappoint. Contacting him at +94 762726799 was a breeze. One piece of advice- those with sensitive airways could do well with some masks because of the trailing dust from a jeep ahead of you on those dry jungle tracks.

review_text:
This park really needs to change the way they do safaris and limit the amount of vehicles in the park. The problem is that they allow hotels to arrange safaris--which all compete with each, this results in an abundance of vehicles in the park with only 1-2 people. So when you see a family of elephants, too many vehicles swarm around them, prohibiting the animals from moving in the direction they want, and causing them to be stressed. Furthermore, with so many vehicles in one area, the exhaust smell is strong and the engines are loud---also not good for the elephants. The park also needs to be stricter with the drivers by reminding them to keep distance and respect the animals.

We all found this experience to be very troubling. I highly suggest when you book your safari, try booking through the park itself, and ask to be put with others in vehicles to limit them in the park. These animals need to be respected in their living space.

review_text:
We had a fantastic half-day safari where we spotted elephants, buffalo, deer, crocodiles, and a gazillion peacocks and other cool birds. We booked through our hotel and had an excellent guide who was very knowledgeable and could spot a green parrot in a tree from 20 metres! From reading other reviews it seems like you get what you pay for. 
When we were queuing we were worried about all the other vehicles around us but when we got into the park everyone went their separate ways. Maybe we were lucky, however - corona virus and the time of year meaning fewer tourists than usual. Also, I imagine some of the roads we drove down would be impassable in the wet season, forcing all the jeeps onto a few larger roads.
All in all, I loved it and got the chance to see elephants in the wild.

review_text: We just returned from a tour of the park with lahira prasad. I was hesitant at first to keep my booking with him as his price was more than the others and I wasn't sure it would be worth it but due to all the good reviews on here we decided to spend the extra Â£20 (figured if you're coming all this way Â£20 is nothing to get a good experience!) Lahira organised a taxi from Ella which picked us up at 4am (need to do the safari whilst it's still cool to see the most animals)him and his driver gave us some light snacks and water and we started the tour. Straight away we saw a small family of elephants including a very small baby! We then went off and toured the park away from all the other "jeeps". Lahira s 4 x4 is the only one powerful enough to get to parts of the parks where nowhere else can go. We saw lots more than the other vehicles who had to stay on the main tracks (crocodile s close up and more elephants)At one point lahira had to help two jeeps that got stuck in the mud....his 4 x4 made light work of it and they had been stuck for a while (the people on the two jeeps that got stuck did not look happy!) Then we whizzed through with no effort at all! Brilliant day and an amazing experience. We then had transfers to mirissa and was there for midday!

review_text:
This was more like harassing elephants than spotting them in an eco friendly way. Imagine at least 20 vehicles converging on a herd of elephants & another 20 on their way. It was like a circus.

The Jeep I went with could have taken another couple but instead they put them in a Jeep of their own & there were plenty of others with sole occupants. This highlighted that it was a more a money making initiative for each driver than for the mental well being of the elephants. I have more vehicles in my photos than elephants. It is not something I will ever do again EVER. The poor elephants having to put up with all that Â‘in your faceÂ’ stuff, with some being quite distressed due to a constant stream of vehicles blocking their paths. It left me feeling appalled that I even did it.

It was wrong on a number of fronts. Firstly their is the mental health of the poor elephants to consider, then of course you have all those vehicles (car pooling is not considered), ripping up the environment, fuel consumption & exhaust contributing to the greenhouse gas emissions, should I go on. So it definitely was not environmentally friendly in so many ways. If you are considering going then consider the above.

review_text:
While researching for our Sri Lanka Trip in November 2019, we came across Lahiru. He is a local tour guide and was recommended on trip advisor and other platforms. We contacted him via WhatsApp around two weeks before the desired day of Safari and agreed on the following:

- Taxi pick up in Ella 4:15 AM
- 3-4 hour Safari in Udawalawe National Park
- Taxi drop off at hotel near Galle

Contact with him in English was easy and everything worked out as expected. The Safari with both transports was very well organised and allowed us to combine the travel from Ella to Galle with the Safari.

The Safari was absolutely amazing and we spent four hours in the national park and saw numerous animals - especially elephants. Lahiru is an excellent guide and we were over and over again surprised how fast he was able to spot different animals. He shares his excellent knowledge during the tour and is very patient with us foreigners that are stunned by the animals.

Overall an awesome experience and we can surely recommend a Safari with Lahiru.

Just get in touch with him via WhatsApp: +94 76 272 6799

review_text:
We had a brilliant safari this morning with Lahiru at Udawalawe National Park.

We were picked up from our hotel in Ella at 4.30 by LahiruÂ’s driver and taken to Udawalawe. From there we jumped in the Land Rover and started the safari. Within a few minutes we saw some elephants not too far from the side of the road, then within another few minutes we saw a single male elephant right next to the road. We couldnÂ’t believe it! 

Lahiru was keen to make sure we saw as much as we could and had plenty of time to get photographs. He pointed out everything he saw including Chameleons hiding on branches. His driver turned the engine off when we got near any animals so we could take our time to photograph them or just stare in amazement. 

Apart from on the main toad we only saw other safari vehicles twice. The vehicle we went in was a Land Rover which meant we could go off the main roads people usually take and went down to the lake, lots of the other vehicles canÂ’t do this because of the wet ground. 

Towards the end of our safari we came across some more Elephants, we stopped briefly and headed past them to a lake to see the crocodiles before the sun got too hot. Then we went back to where the elephants were and just patiently sat while they got nearer to us, and we realised they had a baby with them. It was the most amazing thing, just being able to sit and watch them and being so close to them. 

We would highly recommend Lahiru to anyone thinking about doing a safari.

Other animals we saw include water buffaloes, land monitors, deer, Jackels, lots of birds including king fishers, crested eagle and loads of peacocks. 

After our safari the driver took us onwards to Mirissa. Doing a day trip was perfect and it was brilliant that we were picked up and dropped off so we didnÂ’t need to worry about transport. 

If youÂ’ve not got much time in Sri Lanka donÂ’t miss this day trip! Just drop him a WhatsApp message: +94 76 272 6799.

Thanks again - Adam & Amber

We visited the park on an evening safari beginning at 2pm and finishing at 5pm. I highly recommend making sure you are there as late (or as early) as possible as a number of animals came out towards the end of the tour as it cooled down.

Tour was great and the driver was very experienced and was able to show us a number of different animals long before we could see anything (wild cat, lizards, monkeys, birds, Â‘bambiÂ’ and as expected plenty of elephants). It was definitely worth the trip.

Only four stars though because these tours have a long way to go to meet the price they charge. All the vehicles follow each other in the park and you almost go up the same route you came down, and only experience a small part of the park. If they were to replicate the safariÂ’s in Africa I have been lucky enough to experience they would benefit from two way radioÂ’s in the car (so they can communicate when they see something), a guide to provide info on the history and about the animals and sealed roads to cover larger areas (where is the money going from all these tours??). This would allow them to cover more of the park and enhance the experience for the consumer.

My wife and I went on an afternoon safari with Chaminda, we were very specific that we wanted a quieter tour not harassing animals etc and staying away from the other jeeps where possible. Chaminda to his credit was very professional and careful in his driving and approach of the animals and birds that i think we saw much more than other jeeps that seemed to be racing around. Our guide was very informative, spotting the following:
Blue tailed bee eater 
Malabar pied hornbill
Peahens and peacocks
Brown headed barbet
Mongoose
Little green bee eater 
White bellied sea eagle
Changeable hawk eagle
Coppersmith barbet
Red vented bulbul
Green pigeon
Imperial pigeon 
Sri Lanka green pigeon
Sirkeer malkoha
Crested serpent eagle
Rose ringed Parakeets 
Brown shrike
Indian blue Robyn
water buffalos wallowing in a pond 
And of course elephants, some with very young calves. The highlight of our tour was the pied hornbills as I believe these are shy birds so rare sighting.
Overall a very enjoyable and informative tour. 
I can highly recommend Chaminda, give him a ring or text phone No: +94773379470.
Cheers Michael and Asha, from Darwin Australia.

review_text: After reading other reviews we decided to book directly with Lahiru and we were delighted with our trip. We saw so many elephants including several family groups with baby elephants as young as 2 weeks. We saw lots of other animals and roamed the park on our own, without a flock of jeeps following us.  It was so beautiful and peaceful. We saw water buffaloes, golden hyenas, two types of monkeys, a crocodile, wild pigs, star tortoise and many amazing birds including the beautiful bee catcher. Lahiru speaks brilliant English, has a sense of humour  and is very knowledgeable about the park and the animals.  Highly recommended. Contact Lahiru on whatÂ’s app +94 76 272 6799 to find out more.

review_text:
A must do experience wherever you are in Sri Lanka...we used a reputable courier to book the jeep hire and park fees which cost approximately Â£70. Pay the bit extra for the more expensive jeep which is more substantially equipped than the cheaper model...believe me, you'll be glad of it on the parks trails, which are very very unstable! 
Our guide was very informative and pointed out things we would have easily missed, they are incredibly professional and well informed, not to mention exceptional drivers! Within minutes we were in the company of a majestic bull elephant who seemed quite undeterred by our proximity! 
We booked a couple of hours in the park, enough time to get up close and personal with the famous residents, including deer, water buffalo and a vast array of birds, lizards and mongoose, perhaps a longer tour might have increased our chances of seeing more than the 5 or 6 elephant we did, but by then we'd been bounced around enough! 
This is well worth the fee and advisable early start, if just to be that close to these magnificent creatures.

review_text:
I had the most fantastic day with Chaminda, and recommend him wholeheartedly. He is polite, professional, sensitive to travellersÂ’ needs and speaks pretty good English. He knows the names of all the animals in English and has reference books in the jeep. Most importantly he is knowledgeable about the creatures in the park and has a very good eye for spotting all manner of birds, mammals, and lizards. 

You can call him directly on his mobile 
+94 (077) 337 9470

Chaminda charged me the standard rate for each half day game drive (currently 5,000 rupees) and freely gave me extra time on the morning drive in order to arrive early and beat the long queues, and then added more free extra time at the end too, as he was trying to find a brown fish owl. He spotted so many rare birds for me, and the brown fish owl eluded us on this trip! 

The afternoons are best for elephants as itÂ’s too hot for birds until late afternoon, when visitors have to exit the park. 
Here are some of the notable sightings we had over the day:

Brown Shrike 
Yellow eyed babbler (rare)
Woolly neck stork
Blue faced malkohas (rare)
Sirkeer malkohas (rare)
Red breasted green pigeon
Indian roller
Jungle prinia 
Sikri
Great coucal 
Grey headed fish eagle
Kingfisher (common and black capped)
Chestnut headed bee eater
Little green bee eater
Blue tailed bee eater
Land monitor lizard 
Painted storks
Plum headed parakeet pair (rare)
Hoopoe
Crocodiles

Serpent eagle
Sri Lankan Green pigeon
Tufted Grey langur
Toque Macaques 
Mogoose pair
Yellow water lapwing 
Golden jackal 

Plus common: 
Many elephants including little babies, lots of fascinating behaviours to observe
Peacocks
Water buffaloes 
Egrets
Brahminy kites

review_text: We did a morning trip and this is a very well organised trip with many companies- perhaps too many as most of the vehicles had 1 or 2 people in , this is nice as you get plenty of space but not good for the environment as you could easily reduce the   Impact to both the park and reduce the pollution . Nether the less this place is definitely worth a visit with plenty of wildlife about . We were lucky enough to see a croc ( briefly) , plenty of birds , elephants galore , a mongoose , spiky tortoise , jackals and a curious monkey . Seeing a 2 week old elephant with its mum and 5 yr old sister at a watering hole was the highlight of our holiday ! review_text:
I didn't really want to book a tour with Lahiru because it seems like everyone's reviews are about him and his prices keep going up. But we really had a great experience with Lahiru!! I would highly recommend him.
We saw elephants up so close but really felt like Lahiru respected the animals. We didn't see huge amounts of elephants but saw approx 5 different groups along with water buffalo, crocodiles (!), lizards and 15 different birds. Lahiru's ability to spot wildlife can only come from years of experience. 
Whenever we came across another jeep, Lahiru went another way so we had a truly private tour the whole 4 hours. We had heard about Lahiru taking photos through his binoculars and I hadn't thought much of it. But Lahiru was so skilled at taking photos with your own phone/camera that you could just focus of looking at the wildlife rather than trying to take a good photo.
Lahiru arranged pick up from Ella and then we were dropped off at a beach in the south after the tour. He even organised an extra driver from Ella in the morning because a land slide had blocked a road and the extra driver could navigate a different route.
The whole day cost 250 USD for three people. We booked via Whatsapp (+94762726799). Lahiru also brought food for us (but we didn't know that was going to happen so we had brought our own!).

review_text:
After having been on safari in Botswana, this was a total let down. We ultimately only saw elephants, peacocks, and a bunch of birds. Our whole group got tired of seeing peacocks, and there wasn't much else to see. More annoyingly, the park felt small and we'd constantly be around 5-7 jeeps at a time circling around an animal. It felt unnatural and unkind to the animal.

If you've never been on safari though, I'd recommend it as a great way to spend a morning (no more than four hours is needed). The elephants are a delight to see and it's great to be in nature. The peacocks are very pretty too.

review_text:
We booked our safari through Mansala Safari House and went for the full day option. At the park entrance, we were greeted by Lionel, one of the volunteer guides (note that this is an additional cost) and we are very happy to have had him with us - he has eagle eyes, quite literally, as he pointed out eagles and other wild birds we would otherwise have missed, and even spotted small lizards high up in trees and a tiny musk deer deep in the undergrowth.

Elephants, of course, are easier to spot and we met plenty along the way. Our driver and guide were both fairly respectful of their space, and although all the vehicles in the park are quite noisy, the wildlife in general seemed relatively undisturbed.

In the afternoon, we were incredibly excited to see a leopard and as there were no other jeeps around, we stood for 5 to 10 minutes observing him. Something I think weÂ’ll never forget! Our guide and driver were almost as excited as we were by this rare sighting. It was clearly our lucky day, as we later came across a jungle cat.

IÂ’d heartily recommend a visit to the Udawalawe National Park and if you stay at the Mansala Safari House, they send you off with the most delicious lunch, even catering for vegans like us! 

Total cost for two people in one jeep, with driver, was USD 130 (23,400 LKR). LionelÂ’s services were additional, with a voluntary and discretionary contribution.
